1 # Per-project maintenance scheduling — design 2 3 Status: **agreed** (owner decisions recorded in §11; revised per owner review on 4 PR #391). Supersedes, once migrated, the central fleet routine 5 ([`routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md`](../../routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md) 6 and its external CCR trigger) and the two out-of-band GCEC CCR triggers. 7 The phased rollout lives in [MIGRATION.md](MIGRATION.md). Refs #390. 8 9 The shape: every repo schedules **itself** — a vendored hourly **scheduler Action** 10 evaluates task preconditions and dispatches agent work as `ready-for-agent` issues; 11 a per-repo **executor routine**, fired by that label event, executes them. Work that 12 is genuinely fleet-scoped becomes ordinary tasks *of the canon repo* on the same 13 machinery — no separate central mechanism survives. 14 15 --- 16 17 ## 1. Task anatomy — the pack folder 18 19 `run_daily/` is superseded by `tasks/`, one directory per task, in canon packs 20 and local packs alike: 21 22 ``` 23 packs//tasks// 24 task.mjs # declaration + precondition — self-contained, importable standalone 25 task.md # the worker spec the agent executes; the dispatch issue's first line points here 26 *.sh, *.js # optional deterministic helper scripts (the routine-folder convention, absorbed) 27 ``` 28 29 > **As-built (Phase 0, #396):** `tasks/` lands **additively** — a canon pack 30 > carries both `tasks/` and its untouched `run_daily/` through the rollout, so 31 > the legacy central planner keeps working while the scheduler discovers `tasks/` 32 > from disk (`pack.mjs` is not touched). `run_daily/` is removed only at Phase 4. 33 > The two conformance guards for this shape (`task-declaration-shape`, 34 > `scheduler-workflow-shape`) live in the **basics** pack, not a separate one — 35 > scheduling is baseline discipline (see 36 > [`packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md`](../../packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md)). 37 38 Alongside this migration, `.claudinite/local_packs/` is renamed to 39 `.claudinite/local/packs/` (owner decision, §11): packs then sit at one uniform 40 depth under a single scan root, `.claudinite/*/packs/`. The two valid task-file 41 prefixes in a consumer repo are exactly: 42 43 ``` 44 .claudinite/shared/packs//tasks//task.md (vendored canon task) 45 .claudinite/local/packs//tasks//task.md (project-owned task) 46 ``` 47 48 The canonical local-pack declaration token becomes `local/` (the legacy 49 `local_packs/` and bare-id forms stay accepted, and baselining's 50 normalization rewrites them — same machinery as the 2026-07-19 namespace 51 migration). 52 53 `task.mjs` carries the whole contract: 54 55 ```js 56 export default { 57 id: 'growth-extract', 58 frequency: 'daily-1h', // hourly | daily-2h | daily-1h | daily | daily+1h | weekly | monthly — nothing else 59 precondition_signals: ['commits', 'prs', 'issues'], // which parts of the signals object to collect 60 agent_model: 'opus', // opus | sonnet | haiku | none — 'none' = pure code, no agent, no issue 61 expected_outcome: 'merged-pr', // none | open-pr | merged-pr — the task's write ceiling (§4) 62 agent_instructions: 'task.md', 63 precondition(signals, config) { 64 // Pure code over the collected signals + this pack's entry config from .claudinite-checks.json. 65 // Decides "needs to run" AND emits binding context for the dispatch issue. 66 return { 67 run: true, 68 reason: '2 substantive commits in window', 69 context: ['Only PRs #12 and #15 are in scope. #13 is a bot bump — do not touch it.'], 70 }; 71 }, 72 } 73 ``` 74 75 - **`frequency`** — exactly the seven values above. `daily±Nh` offsets the repo's 76 daily anchor hour (§2); weekly/monthly fire at the anchor hour on the configured day. 77 - **`precondition_signals`** — the scheduler collects only the union of what the *due* tasks 78 declare; a non-daily slot never pays for daily tasks' signals. 79 - **`agent_model`** — family names, resolved to a concrete model id in **one** vendored 80 module (`engine/scheduler/model-map.mjs`), so a model-generation bump is one 81 edit. `none` replaces `smarts: 'none'`: the worker is an `.mjs` the scheduler 82 runs inline — no issue, no agent. 83 - **`expected_outcome`** — a declared **ceiling**, not a promise: `none` may never open a 84 PR, `open-pr` may open but never merge, `merged-pr` may arm auto-merge. "No 85 change" is always a legal result. Enforced post-hoc by the executor in code, 86 not just requested in prose. A repo whose `maintenance.delivery` is `review` 87 degrades `merged-pr` tasks to `open-pr` — member config wins. Pushes to 88 non-default branches (e.g. the `conversation-logs` prune) are outside the 89 taxonomy. 90 - **`precondition`** — today's `gate` renamed. It both asserts need-to-run and 91 **pre-decides scope**: `context` lines land verbatim in the dispatch issue, and 92 the executor treats them as constraints the agent may not re-litigate (if the 93 precondition can rule a PR irrelevant in code, the agent never re-decides it). 94 A precondition is cheap and local: decision logic and API reads/writes only — 95 never network fetches of external pages, never long work (see the 96 create-extractor row in §6 for the boundary in practice). 97 - Per-task project settings ride the already-sanctioned container — the pack 98 entry's `config` in `.claudinite-checks.json`. No new per-task engine keys. 99 - The self-contained-module rule carries over: `task.mjs` imports nothing, so 100 scheduler, executor, and humans load it standalone. Local pack dir-name == id 101 stays load-bearing. 102 103 ## 2. Repo-level schedule settings 104 105 New top-level key in `.claudinite-checks.json` (added to the engine's closed 106 `CONFIG_KEYS` set): 107 108 ```json 109 "taskScheduler": { "dailyHour": 4, "weeklyDay": "Sun", "monthlyDay": 1 } 110 ``` 111 112 All values **UTC** (requirements normalize to UTC at the door). Defaults when 113 absent: `dailyHour: 4`, `weeklyDay: "Sun"`, `monthlyDay: 1`. `monthlyDay` clamps 114 to the month's last day; `daily-2h` with `dailyHour < 2` wraps into the previous 115 calendar day (the slot keeps the anchor's date). With the default anchor the four 116 daily slots stage the whole growth chain in order: 117 118 ``` 119 02:00 daily-2h baselining (+ migrations-apply) ─ own mount converged before anything reads it 120 03:00 daily-1h extract (activity + conversation) ─ lessons captured from a converged repo 121 04:00 daily promote (canon repo) ─ lifts the night's merged extracts to canon 122 Sun 04:00 weekly dedup ─ prunes against the mounted (merged) canon 123 ``` 124 125 The stages couple through *merged* upstream state, not a barrier: extract's 126 auto-merge PR usually lands well within the hour before promote reads it, and 127 dedup reads only the merged/mounted canon (never an in-flight promote PR), so the 128 ordering is freshness staging that mostly holds and self-heals to next-day 129 propagation when a merge lags. 130 131 > **As-built (owner, 2026-08-01): the staging holds only while the fires do — so one task can 132 > take the run.** The hour between anchors is not a barrier, and it is not a 133 > guarantee either: a GitHub `schedule:` fire is dropped and delayed freely (see 134 > the `github-actions-scheduling` skill), and a run that fires at 05:40 after 135 > three dropped fires finds all four daily slots due at once. Every one of them 136 > dispatches together, so **baselining runs beside the tasks whose ground it 137 > exists to repair** rather than an hour ahead of them — and baselining is not 138 > freshness staging like the rest of the chain, it is the pass that converges the 139 > mount, the wiring and the migration notes the others then execute against. 140 > 141 > On those runs the ordering has to be asserted rather than implied. A 142 > precondition may return **`exclusive: true`** beside `run: true` — *if I run 143 > this cycle, I run alone* — and the scheduler defers every other due task 144 > (§3, step 4). Baselining claims it exactly when the mount is genuinely overdue: 145 > more than a day since the last converge landed, and not more than three (past 146 > that the repo is wedged — an unmerged maintenance PR, a broken converge — which 147 > is a human's problem, and holding the rest of the repo back another night does 148 > not fix it). The routine same-day case claims nothing, so the common night is 149 > unchanged. 150 > 151 > **A deferred slot is spent, not queued.** Due-ness is `slotTime ∈ (lastSuccess, 152 > now]` and the claiming run *succeeds*, so the watermark moves past the slot it 153 > deferred: a deferred daily task runs at tomorrow's slot, a weekly one next 154 > week. That is the accepted price — the alternative is running the nightly chain 155 > against a mount that baselining has not yet fixed. The run says so in its 156 > summary (`defer —`) and its run record (`deferred`), so the cost is counted 157 > rather than silent. 158 159 > **As-built (#582): dedup left the nightly chain for the weekly anchor.** It was 160 > designed at `daily+1h` (05:00), an hour after promote. But a member's mount moves 161 > most nights — baselining converges it daily — so the `sharedMount` arm fired this 162 > opus dispatch, and the owner-gated PR behind it, nearly every night, for prunes 163 > nobody is waiting on: a local item the canon has already absorbed stays harmlessly 164 > correct until it goes. Nothing is missed by the move, because its signals are 165 > **window-scoped** (§3.3) and the window is the widest due task's period — the 166 > weekly run sees a full 7 days of movement, batched into one dispatch. The staging 167 > that mattered survives: that morning's 02:00 baselining converges the mount before 168 > dedup reads it at 04:00. The 05:00 ordering behind promote never bought freshness 169 > anyway — a promotion reaches a member only once *its* baselining pulls it in, 170 > which is a later day regardless. 171 172 ## 3. The scheduler — one vendored hourly Action per repo 173 174 `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` (vendored stub, shape-enforced by a 175 conformance check): hourly cron on a **repo-hashed minute constrained to 176 :10–:50** (spreads the fleet, dodges GitHub's :00 stampede, and keeps clear of 177 the hour boundary the slot math anchors on), `workflow_dispatch` for manual 178 runs, a `concurrency` group serializing runs. The workflow itself is a thin shim 179 — all logic lives in the vendored engine, so the file under `.github/` changes 180 rarely (a property to preserve: schema and behavior changes ride the vendor 181 refresh, not workflow edits). It runs 182 `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/run.mjs`, which: 183 184 1. **Decides due slots statelessly from the run ledger GitHub already keeps.** 185 For each frequency, compute the most recent scheduled slot time ≤ now from 186 `taskScheduler`. Fetch the timestamp `T` of this workflow's last **successful** run 187 (Actions API). A slot is due iff its time ∈ `(T, now]`. 188 - Miss/outage → the next successful run catches up daily/weekly/monthly slots; 189 no watermark file, nothing to corrupt. 190 - Only the most recent slot per frequency is considered → a 3-day outage 191 yields one catch-up evaluation, never a backfill storm. 192 - **Hourly slots never catch up** (stale polls are worthless). 193 - Late fire (15:02 for a ~15:00 slot) is irrelevant — due-ness is schedule 194 math, never wall-clock equality. 195 - No prior success (fresh adoption) → the most-recent slots of the **first-run 196 set** are due: `hourly` plus the daily family, never weekly or monthly. The 197 first run is an adoption smoke test, and the wiring it proves — discovery, 198 signals, dispatch issue, label, executor pickup — is the same whatever the 199 frequency, so the daily family exercises all of it. Adding weekly/monthly 200 would only buy an off-anchor run of their unconditional tasks (open-web 201 research, pack discovery, the fleet sweep) on the least-proven repo in the 202 fleet; they wait for their real anchor, which is due normally once this run 203 is in the ledger. 204 - An **unreadable** ledger is not an empty one. `T = null` is a positive claim 205 that the repo has never run, so the read returns it only for a 200 that 206 found no successful run; a non-2xx (or a run record with no timestamp) 207 throws and the run **fails**, evaluating nothing. Failing is free here — 208 a failed run never enters the success ledger, so `T` stays put and the next 209 successful run catches up the missed slots by the same outage rule above. 210 An exit-0 abort would not be free: it would enter the ledger and advance `T` 211 past the slots it declined to evaluate. 212 2. **Discovers tasks** with one uniform scan — 213 `.claudinite/{shared,local}/packs/

/tasks/*/task.mjs` — activation-gated by 214 the `packs` declaration exactly like checks and skills; filters to due 215 frequencies. 216 3. **Collects signals** — only the declared union. Vocabulary (one collector 217 module each; window = the task's period + 1h slack, stateless fixed lookback; 218 overlap absorbed by dedupe): 219 - `commits` — default-branch commits in window, `substantiveChange` 220 classification, touched paths. 221 - `prs`, `issues`, `branches` — open + touched-in-window. `branches` carries 222 `touched` by reading each distinct tip sha's commit date (one read per tip; 223 no REST branch listing carries a date), because before that it carried 224 *names only* — leaving the branch dimension with no notion of newness and 225 every gate over it degenerate to "a branch exists". An unreadable tip is 226 `updatedAt: null`, never touched. `prs` additionally 227 carries `merged`, the PRs **merged during the window** (the review 228 discussion behind a change is the richest lesson material there is, and it 229 is closed by the time a window sees it). `merged` is a separate field, not 230 folded into `open`/`touched`, so widening it cannot widen the target set of 231 a task that sweeps the open PRs. Self-trigger exclusions carried over **and 232 extended**: the housekeeping-commit regex, tracker titles, and now 233 `[claudinite-task]` issues and `ready-for-agent` label events are invisible 234 to signals. 235 - `release` — latest GitHub release + manifest version. 236 - `localPacks` — present / changed-in-window. 237 - `sharedMount` — which *declared* packs' vendored files changed in the 238 window. Replaces the cross-repo `relevantCanonChanged`: the member's own 239 merged vendor-refresh commit is the local echo of "canon changed". 240 - `conversationLogs` — logs branch present, oldest JSONL age vs retention. 241 - `stamp` — the `claudinite.updated`/`ref` provenance stamp and its age; 242 plus the canon head sha when the canon is readable from the Action 243 (baselining's precondition falls back to stamp-age when it isn't). 244 - `fleet` — canon repo only, over the fleet PAT (the members aggregate for 245 the genuinely fleet-scoped tasks). Consumers cannot declare it. 246 A **manual** `workflow_dispatch` run may additionally carry `overrides` — one 247 free-form `KEY=value` string, since GitHub cannot declare arbitrary named 248 inputs. It reaches the engine as `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`, and the engine 249 understands exactly one key: **`FORCE_TASKS=`**. 250 A forced task is put in the due list under its most-recent slot **and runs 251 without its precondition being consulted at all** — forcing is a decision the 252 operator already made, so nothing asks the task whether it agrees, and no task 253 declaration mentions forcing anywhere (#515). The engine learns "run these 254 ids", never what any of them do. An id matching no discovered task forces 255 nothing; a task due on its own merit is judged normally, not forced; and a 256 forced dispatch carries a generic Context saying so, since its issue Context 257 is the agent's binding scope and nothing here asserts there is work to do. 258 259 The case it exists for is `FORCE_TASKS=baselining`: the age gate 260 (`ageDays > 1`) means a repo that baselined this morning is not due again for 261 over a day, so a canon fix worth propagating *today* otherwise had no lever 262 short of hand-editing each repo's stamp. The two gates are why forcing has to 263 live in the engine: the SLOT gate runs before any precondition, so an override 264 a task read for itself was unreachable on exactly the mid-day run that needs 265 it. 266 267 4. **Runs preconditions** — pure code, per-task try/catch isolation; a throwing 268 precondition converges to the standard failure state (`report-failure` 269 composite → `workflow-failure` issue); other tasks proceed. Every due task's 270 verdict is computed **before** anything is dispatched, because of the next 271 point: a claim on the run is only knowable once they have all spoken. 272 273 A verdict may carry **`exclusive: true`** beside `run: true` — *if I run this 274 cycle, I run alone* — and every other due task whose precondition said run is 275 **deferred**: no preprocessing subprocess, no dispatch issue, no inline work 276 (owner, 2026-08-01). It exists because the hourly cron is not hourly: a run that fires 277 hours late finds several daily slots due at once and dispatches the whole 278 nightly chain together, which puts baselining *beside* the tasks whose mount 279 it exists to converge instead of an hour ahead of them (§2 as-built). The 280 engine learns "this verdict claims the run", never which task claims it or 281 why — the same separation `FORCE_TASKS` keeps, and the reason no engine module 282 mentions baselining. Two claimants are not a conflict: they both run and 283 everything else defers, so no priority order between packs is needed. A 284 **forced** task is exempt from deferral and cannot claim (its verdict is the 285 engine's, not the task's) — a claim swallowing the task the operator asked for 286 would make a hand-started run do nothing it was started for. 287 288 A deferred slot is **spent, not queued**: this run succeeds, so the watermark 289 moves past it and the task runs again at its *next* slot (tomorrow, or next 290 week). That cost is the point of bounding who may claim — see §2. 291 5. **Executes or dispatches** — `model: 'none'` → run the worker `.mjs` inline 292 (which may itself dispatch and await another workflow); otherwise file the 293 dispatch issue (§4) labeled `ready-for-agent`. A deferred task does neither. 294 6. **Reports** — the job summary lists every evaluated task with run/skip/reason 295 (the observability `plan.json` used to give). Whole-run failure escalates per 296 `gha/scheduled-failure-escalation`. Beside the prose, the run prints one 297 **machine-readable record per evaluated task** — `claudinite-task-run v1 298 / [] `, outcome ∈ `agent` / `preprocess` / 299 `skipped` / `failed` / `deferred` (`run-record.mjs`, the single home of both 300 the renderer and its parser). Printed *after* the action loop, so it states 301 what happened rather than what was planned. Nothing in the scheduler reads it 302 back — it exists so the usage aggregation can count task invocations without 303 the scheduler acquiring state of its own (skill-usage-metrics DESIGN §4.2). 304 305 `fullSweep`, `full_sweep_supported`, and the hash-stagger retire: "weekly" is now 306 a declaration, not a gate trick. And the scheduler is **the only cron in the 307 repo** — the release workflow's independent 00:30 cron is absorbed into the 308 store-release task (§6), so recurring work has exactly one trigger surface. 309 310 ## 4. The dispatch issue — exactly-once, bounded, recoverable 311 312 - **Title**: `[claudinite-task] / `; slot-id 313 `h2026-07-22T14Z` (hourly), `d2026-07-22` (daily family), `w2026-07-19` 314 (weekly, the slot's day), `m2026-07` (monthly). 315 - **Body** — first line is the task-file path; everything behavior-defining 316 (model, outcome, worker content) is read from the tracked repo file, never 317 from the issue: 318 319 ``` 320 .claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/create-extractor/task.md 321 322 Execute the Claudinite task above (pack `gcec`, task `create-extractor`, slot `h2026-07-22T14Z`). 323 The Context section below is binding scope — do not re-decide it. 324 325 ### Context 326 - Eligible requests: #123, #125. #124 is labeled extractor-blocked-needs-human — do not touch it. 327 ``` 328 - **Exactly-once per (task, slot)**: before creating, search issues state=**all** 329 for the exact title; found → skip. Makes scheduler double-runs and 330 crash-retries safe (`concurrency` serializes; the search closes the 331 crashed-mid-run window). 332 - **At-most-one open issue per task**: any open `[claudinite-task] /` 333 issue (any slot) suppresses new filings — an executor outage accumulates zero 334 backlog beyond one issue per task. An open dispatch issue older than ~2 of its 335 periods gets an escalation comment + `needs-human` from the scheduler. 336 - **Lifecycle**: success → executor comments the result and closes it. Failure → 337 comment naming what failed, remove `ready-for-agent`, add `needs-human`. 338 Every exit converges to one visible triage state (the canon's 339 failure-convergence rule — which also fixes create-extractor's current 340 "trigger label never removed" gap). 341 342 ## 5. The executor — a per-repo routine fired by the `ready-for-agent` label 343 344 One CCR routine per repo (owner decision, §11), created at bootstrap, 345 **triggered by the GitHub issue event of the `ready-for-agent` label being 346 applied** — not by a timer. The session starts when the scheduler labels the 347 issue, so dispatch latency is the session spin-up, minutes not hours, and no 348 sessions burn on empty hours. 349 350 - **Session model**: `sonnet` — the routine itself only orchestrates; each task 351 runs as a **subagent at the task's declared model family** (how per-task model 352 survives a single-model routine). 353 - **Launcher prompt** (thin pointer, per the unattended-agents rule): 354 `Execute the Claudinite executor: .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/executor.md`. 355 - **Session sources** are the **member repo alone** (agent-preprocessing DESIGN 356 §7/E5). The executor no longer needs the canon checkout: baselining fetches 357 PUBLIC canon **Action-side** in its `agent_preprocessing` worker and reads 358 migration notes from the member's own vendored mount, so a project-only session 359 is all the ambient scope executor work requires. (Superseded the earlier model, 360 where the canon rode in the session sources so the baselining task could run the 361 canon's vendoring script directly.) 362 - **`executor.md`** (vendored, hyper-specific, MCP-only GitHub access): 363 1. **The triggering issue is the session's *only* work item.** It never lists or 364 processes another open `ready-for-agent` issue. 365 366 This is the fix for the duplicate-execution bug. One scheduler run files every 367 due task's dispatch issue seconds apart, each already labeled, so **one run 368 emits one label event per issue and starts one session per event**. The 369 original design paired that fan-out with a self-healing sweep in which every 370 session also drained its siblings — so N dispatches produced N sessions each 371 building the same N-issue work list. The step-3 claim could not save it: every 372 session read the list before any of them claimed. Observed on 2026-07-26 — 373 dispatch #427 run twice (#452), #425 run three times, leaving four duplicate 374 tracker issues, three duplicate filings of one finding, and duplicate PRs 375 making the same changes. 376 377 One session, one issue: concurrency between sessions stays normal and becomes 378 safe by construction. The recovery the sweep provided moves into deterministic 379 scheduler code (below). 380 381 Steps 1 and 2 are one command: `resolve-dispatch.mjs` does both, so neither 382 the identification nor the validation depends on the session's judgment. 383 384 **The trigger reaches the session by two transports, and both are read.** 385 GitHub Actions writes the webhook payload to `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` (number + 386 label + body, one shot). Claude Code on the web writes no payload file and 387 instead sets `CCR_TRIGGER_SOURCE` / `CCR_TRIGGER_EVENT` / `CCR_TRIGGER_REPO` 388 / `CCR_TRIGGER_ISSUE_NUMBER`, which name the issue but carry neither its 389 labels nor its body — so that path resolves in two shots (`needs-issue`, 390 exit 13: the executor fetches that one issue over MCP, saves the raw 391 response JSON verbatim, and re-invokes with `--issue-json`; the shell 392 extracts body/labels/title itself and rejects a response for the wrong 393 issue number — `--issue-body-file` / `--issue-labels` remain as the manual 394 fallback). Reading only the Actions transport 395 is what let the duplicate-execution bug back in: every CCR-run executor 396 session missed its own trigger, fell through to the fallback, and selected 397 an issue by listing. Observed 2026-07-28, dispatch #772 claimed twice one 398 second apart. 399 400 **There is no fallback, deliberately.** A session that cannot name its 401 trigger runs *nothing* (exit 12) — it never selects a dispatch by listing the 402 queue. That fallback was the same N-sessions-racing-over-N-issues failure as 403 the sweep it replaced, reached from the other direction: every session that 404 cannot identify its trigger builds the same work list, and the claim cannot 405 save them because they all read the list before any of them claims. The 406 scheduler's hourly re-arm is the recovery, in code, once. 407 2. Deterministic validation in code, before any model judgment 408 (`resolve-dispatch.mjs`, over `validate-dispatch.mjs`'s pure core): the body's 409 first line matches 410 `^(\.claudinite\/(shared|local)\/)?packs\/[^/]+\/tasks\/[^/]+\/task\.md$`, 411 the file exists at HEAD, its pack is declared, its `task.mjs` sibling 412 parses; prints the resolved model and outcome ceiling. The shell itself makes 413 no GitHub call on either transport — the body arrives from the payload or 414 from the executor's own MCP fetch — which is what keeps it runnable in the 415 MCP-only, tokenless executor session. Exit codes are the interface: valid / 416 invalid (comment + de-label + `needs-human`) / not-this-scope / needs-issue / 417 no-trigger (stop). 418 3. **Claim** the issue as a *verified lease*, since GitHub offers no 419 compare-and-swap on labels: **read** the current labels and abandon if the 420 ready label is gone or `agent-running`/`needs-human` is present; **swap** 421 `ready-for-agent` → `agent-running` and post a claim comment; **re-read** and, 422 if a second claim comment is present, let the earliest claim win and end the 423 session without dispatching. The read-swap-*confirm* shape is what makes the 424 claim meaningful — the original blind swap could not detect a lost race, and 425 the missing third step is what let a duplicate through. 426 4. Dispatch a subagent at the declared model: read `task.md`, follow it 427 exactly; the issue's Context section is binding scope — never re-decide or 428 widen it. 429 5. Post-verify in code (`verify-outcome.mjs`): outcome ceiling respected (a 430 `none` task that opened a PR, or an `open-pr` task that merged one, fails 431 the run); then close the issue with a result comment, or converge the 432 failure (comment + `needs-human`, remove `agent-running`). 433 6. **No backstop sweeps.** Converging a dead `agent-running` claim, and 434 re-arming a dispatch whose label event never landed, are the **scheduler's**, 435 in code, once per hourly run — not the executor's. Sweeping them here meant 436 every session triggered by the same run swept the same issues in parallel: 437 the duplicate-work bug again, in miniature. 438 439 **The scheduler's maintenance pass** (`run.mjs` `maintainDispatchIssues`, over the 440 pure rules in `dispatch.mjs`) is now the single home for executor recovery. Each 441 hourly run, after filing the cycle's dispatches: 442 443 1. **Stale** — a dispatch open past ~2 of its own scheduling periods → 444 escalation comment, drop the ready label, add `needs-human` 445 (`staleDispatchIssues`; specified since the original design, but never 446 actually wired into `main()` until now). 447 2. **Dead claim** — `agent-running` with no activity for ~3h → comment, drop 448 `agent-running`, add `needs-human` (`staleClaimedDispatchIssues`). Scoped to 449 `[claudinite-task]` titles, so a task's claim on an issue *it* owns is never 450 swept. 451 3. **Re-arm** — armed, unclaimed, uncommented and past a 20-minute grace window 452 → the trigger event was lost, so remove and re-add its own ready label to 453 emit a fresh one (`rearmDispatchIssues`). Remove-then-add is load-bearing: 454 re-applying a label already present emits no `labeled` event. A fleet 455 dispatch re-arms under the fleet label, never the self one. 456 457 Stale wins over re-arm, so an issue converging to triage is never put back into 458 circulation; and stale is what bounds the re-arm loop when the executor is down 459 for good. 460 461 **Security** — this raises the bar; it is not a hard boundary. Applying a label 462 requires triage/write permission, so a drive-by issue filing can't summon the 463 agent — but anyone with write access, or a leaked token that can label, can. 464 The real containment is narrower and structural: the issue never carries 465 instructions. The executor only runs tracked, reviewed task files at 466 code-validated paths, and model/outcome come from the repo, not the issue — so 467 a forged dispatch at worst runs a legitimate task early, inside its declared 468 outcome ceiling. 469 470 **Creation at bootstrap**: the adopting session creates the label-wired routine 471 via the trigger API when available; otherwise it files an owner issue carrying 472 the exact routine config (trigger event, filter label, model, launcher prompt) 473 in one enclosed block — the only human action left in wiring a repo into 474 maintenance. 475 476 ## 6. Task-by-task mapping 477 478 Per-project tasks — run by every declaring repo's own scheduler: 479 480 | Task (pack) | frequency | precondition_signals | agent_model | expected_outcome | Notes | 481 |---|---|---|---|---|---| 482 | baselining (basics) | daily-2h | stamp, sharedMount | sonnet | merged-pr | **Now a per-repo self-refresh, not a fleet pass**: converge own `.claudinite/shared/` to canon head, apply pending migration notes (the old fleet apply pass folds in here), advance the stamp — delivered on the per-cycle `claudinite/maintenance-*` PR, delivery per member config. **Superseded by agent-preprocessing DESIGN §7/E4–E5**: the deterministic converge is now `agent_preprocessing` fetching **public** canon Action-side (no in-session canon checkout — E5 drops canon from the executor's sources), and the agent stage runs only on the nights judgment is left (conditional hand-off). Precondition fires ~daily via the stamp-age fallback (`canonHead` is null now — the worker fetches canon, not the Action). The canon repo skips naturally (no shared mount). | 483 | growth-extract (grow_with_claudinite) | daily-1h | commits, prs, issues, conversationLogs | opus | merged-pr | Precondition = substantiveChange OR a log actually past retention; context = the commit/PR/issue lists **and which halves are live**. **As built: one task over both sources.** Designed (and first built) as two tasks — `growth-extract` over activity, `conversation-extract` over the captured logs — firing in the same 03:00 slot against the same local packs. They share the lesson bar, the promotion ladder and the dedup surface, so the split cost a second opus dispatch, a second PR, and two runs deduping against a corpus the other was concurrently writing. The worker now runs the `extract-from-activity` and `extract-from-conversations` skills in turn, then `prose-to-checks` over the prose it just wrote, and lands all of it in one auto-merging PR. The age-based retention prune still fires correctly on quiet repos — as its own precondition arm, with Context saying the activity half is out of scope. | 484 | growth-dedup (grow_with_claudinite) | weekly | localPacks, sharedMount, commits | opus | open-pr | `relevantCanonChanged` → `sharedMount`; movement, not the calendar, is what wakes it — a quiet repo skips. **Weekly as built (#582), designed `daily+1h`**: a member's mount moves most nights, so the daily slot fired an opus dispatch and an owner-gated PR nightly for prunes nobody waits on. The window-scoped signals batch the week's movement into one run (§2). | 485 | tidy-issues (tidy-repo) | daily | issues, commits | sonnet | none | The undeclared-canon carve-out dies: the canon repo declares tidy-repo like everyone else. **One task per tidy dimension** (the single `repo-tidy` pass split, #481): the acting dimension. Trigger = an issue touched in the window; scope = those issues, widened to every open issue when the default branch ALSO moved substantively — that move is what can make an old issue implemented, so the "full sweep" is signal-triggered, never a calendar flag. The move does not *wake* the task, only widen it: on a repo whose `main` moves most days, waking on it re-triaged every open issue daily. | 486 | tidy-prs (tidy-repo) | weekly | prs | sonnet | none | Assess-only. Gated on an open PR being opened or updated in the window; full whenever it runs (scope = every open PR, since a verdict is relative to the others). A PR verdict is a standing recommendation, not a same-day alert, so the full sweep is the **frequency declaration** — consistent with `fullSweep` retiring in §3. An untouched set of open PRs yields the verdicts already in the tracker, so it is not re-swept. | 487 | tidy-branches (tidy-repo) | weekly | branches | sonnet | none | Assess-only. Gated on a branch being created or pushed in the window (the `branches` signal carries tip dates for exactly this; a push to the default or an infra branch does not count); full whenever it runs, since a branch verdict is relative to the others. Branch cruft accumulates on a weekly clock. Excludes the presumed default names and the infra branches (`conversation-logs`, `claudinite/maintenance`); the worker owns excluding the repo's *real* default branch. | 488 | wiki-growth (product-wiki) | weekly | commits | opus | open-pr | The open-growth-PR preflight is subsumed by the at-most-one-open-issue guard + a precondition check. | 489 | store-release (chrome-extension-release) | daily | release, commits | none | none | **Absorbs the release workflow's independent 00:30 cron**: the precondition detects a deployable change since the last release (or an unreleased manifest bump); the inline worker dispatches the `Release to Chrome Store` workflow in daily mode and awaits it. The workflow becomes push + `workflow_dispatch` only; its conformance check flips from *requiring* the contract cron to *forbidding* any cron. | 490 | create-extractor (gcec, local) | **hourly** | issues | sonnet | open-pr | **Revised by agent-preprocessing (§9), as built.** The *precondition* is only the cheap gate it can be from signals alone: is any open request issue eligible (not already claimed or handed to a human)? Everything deterministic — triage, closing the requests that need no work, branch + scaffold, the page fetch its `required_secrets` pays for, and the draft PR — is `agent_preprocessing`, which needs the issue bodies, GitHub writes, and network fetch a precondition may not do. The agent is requested (conditional hand-off) only when there is genuinely something left to write. The user-facing request issue stays; the dispatch issue references it. | 491 | auto-fallback-coverage (gcec, local) | daily | commits | opus | open-pr | `preconditions.sh` becomes the precondition over `commits`. Fixes the live cadence bug (daily spec vs weekly cron: ~6/7 of windows currently unexamined). | 492 | fleet-freshness (sheepdog) | weekly | none | none | none | **Added after this design, by what this design caused.** Making every member maintain itself removed the last outside look at a member: one whose scheduler was never vendored, was deleted, or was auto-disabled after 60 quiet days is still `covered` to the census and files no failure issue, because nothing runs there to fail — self-maintenance cannot detect its own absence. This sweep probes each covered member's declaration, scheduler workflow, and stamped ref against Claudinite's default branch, and classifies drift by root cause (`no-stamp` → `no-scheduler` → `ref-not-on-trunk` → `behind`), converging `fleet-drift` issues. Same classification as its sibling: an ordinary pack task whose *implementation* spans the fleet. Weekly because drift is measured in days (`staleDays`, default 14); it shares the census's PAT and adds no scope. | 493 | fleet-census (sheepdog) | daily | none | none | none | **An ordinary pack task, not a fleet mechanism**: its *implementation* — preprocessing that runs the census with the account-spanning PAT, declared as `required_secrets` — happens to scan every repo under the owner, but its declaration, scheduling, and lifecycle are exactly those of any pack task. This classification is noted in the sheepdog pack's RULES.md and in the task file itself. (As designed here this was a dispatch-only workflow holding the PAT; #472 folded it into preprocessing, since a workflow existing only to hold a secret is redundant once a task can declare one.) | 494 495 Canon-repo tasks — the canon's own packs on the same machinery. Only three are 496 genuinely fleet-scoped (they need the `fleet` signal / cross-repo reach); the 497 rest of what the old central routine did has moved above: 498 499 | Task | frequency | agent_model | expected_outcome | Fleet-scoped? | Notes | 500 |---|---|---|---|---|---| 501 | growth-promote (canon-curation) | daily | opus | open-pr | yes | Reads members' local packs (`fleet` signal: which members' local packs changed); writes the canon; owner-gated PR. 04:00, after the fleet's 03:00 extracts. | 502 | growth-discover-packs (canon-curation) | weekly | opus | open-pr | yes | Moves from member-scheduled/centrally-executed to plainly central: one weekly sweep over members; first-sight dedup is trivial with a single run. | 503 | migrations-retire (canon-curation) | daily+1h | none | open-pr | yes | Apply evidence is now per-repo (each member's stamp advances when its own baselining applies notes), so the retire guard reads member stamps + `legacyPresent` probes over the `fleet` signal — the same five-condition guard with per-repo stamps replacing the in-memory same-cycle handoff. No artifact plumbing. | 504 | prose-to-checks-sweep (canon-curation) | **daily** | opus | open-pr | no | Not a fleet thing — a canon task going over the canon's own prose. Daily per owner decision. **Weekly as built**, and a per-repo grow_with_claudinite task rather than a canon-local one: growth-extract now runs the same skill over its *own* additions every night, so fresh prose never waits for the sweep and what the sweep sees is a standing backlog that moves on a weekly clock. | 505 506 ## 7. Recoverability semantics (the message-semantics contract) 507 508 - **Scheduler miss** → next successful run catches up non-hourly slots (run-ledger 509 due-ness). **Late/early fire** → irrelevant (schedule math). **Double run** → 510 workflow `concurrency` + exactly-once issue per (task, slot) via state=all 511 title search. 512 - **Missed label event / executor down** → the issue stays labeled and open; the 513 scheduler's next run re-arms it, and escalates it to `needs-human` if it is 514 still unrun past ~2 periods. **Duplicate label events on one issue** → the 515 read-swap-confirm claim lease. **Several issues dispatched at once** → not a 516 race at all: each session runs only its own issue. **Executor died mid-run** → 517 the scheduler converges the stale `agent-running` claim to `needs-human`. 518 - Recovery lives in **one place, in code**. The rule it cost a duplicate-execution 519 incident to learn: when a trigger fans out to N concurrent sessions, never also 520 give each session a sweep over the shared work — every session will do every 521 other session's work, and a claim taken after the work list is read cannot 522 prevent it. 523 - **Precondition/signal crash** → per-task isolation + `workflow-failure` issue; 524 the rest of the run proceeds. 525 - Not idempotence — recoverability: every anomaly lands in a visible, bounded, 526 human-triageable issue state, and issue volume is capped at one open dispatch 527 issue per task by construction. 528 529 ## 8. End state — everything that remains scheduled 530 531 1. **Per repo (identical, vendored)**: `claudinite-scheduler.yml` — **the only 532 cron in the repo** — plus one label-fired executor routine (thin pointer to 533 the vendored `executor.md`). 534 2. **Canon repo only**: the four tasks in §6's second table — ordinary tasks of 535 that repo, three of them fleet-scoped by signal, none by mechanism. 536 3. **Deleted**: the "All Missing Bulb Repos - Daily Maintenance" CCR trigger, 537 both GCEC CCR triggers, `routines/auto-all-repos-maintenance.md`, 538 `routines/fleet/` (planner, registry, local-tasks, schedule, gates, signals), 539 and the release workflow's independent cron. 540 4. **Unchanged**: Yestersummary (out of scope). 541 542 Doctrine rewrite: `scheduling.md`'s "one fleet schedule" becomes "one 543 **scheduler per repo** — the vendored hourly Action is the repo's only cron; 544 agent work is dispatched only through `ready-for-agent` issues; recurring work 545 that used to be its own cron'd workflow becomes a scheduler task, and that 546 workflow is deleted." 547 548 A competing cron is **not** retained as a dispatch-only workflow for a task to 549 fire. That shape keeps two files and two edit sites for one job, and leaves a 550 workflow whose only caller is the thing that replaced it — the task's worker is 551 where the steps belong. The one shape that legitimately survives is a workflow 552 that must run *as an Action* for something a task cannot reach (see 553 `store-release`, §7) — and even then the task owns the schedule, not the 554 workflow. 555 556 ## 9. Bootstrap changes 557 558 Part 6 of `bootstrap.md` (the "Enroll …" owner issue) is **replaced**. 559 Bootstrap now: (a) vendors the scheduler workflow, (b) writes `taskScheduler` defaults 560 into `.claudinite-checks.json`, (c) creates the label-wired executor routine via the 561 trigger API — or files the enclosed-config owner issue when the API isn't reachable. 562 The `ready-for-agent` / `agent-running` / `needs-human` / `workflow-failure` labels 563 need **no** bootstrap step: the scheduler ensures each exists (create-if-missing, 564 idempotent) before it dispatches, so they materialize on the first run and self-heal 565 if deleted — GitHub never creates a label on demand when it is applied, so the 566 assigner guaranteeing it is the correct home for that (the label-create-before-add 567 principle, in code). "A consuming project 568 schedules nothing" flips to "a consuming project schedules **itself**"; 569 baselining's close-the-enrollment-issue step retires; open Enroll issues are 570 closed during migration. 571 572 ## 10. Docs and checks rewritten alongside 573 574 `routines/fleet/scheduling.md` + `DESIGN.md` (new doctrine), 575 `gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor` (rescope: the vendored scheduler workflow is 576 the repo's only permitted cron; a competing cron's work moves into a scheduler 577 task and the workflow is deleted), 578 `chrome-extension-release/release-workflows.mjs` (require **no** cron instead of 579 the contract cron), `in-session-github-access` (unchanged for session-side code 580 — executor + workers stay MCP-only; exempt `engine/scheduler/` Action-side 581 code, which legitimately uses `GITHUB_TOKEN`), the unattended-agents skill 582 (task-folder convention absorbs the routine-folder shape; new rule: issue-driven 583 dispatch security — label-as-authorization, first-line path validation in code, 584 issue content is data), `bootstrap.md` Part 6, `packs/README.md` / 585 `extending.md` (`run_daily` → `tasks`; `local_packs` → `local/packs`), the 586 `local_packs` reference set (engine `LOCAL_PACKS_SUBDIR` / `LOCAL_DECL_PREFIX` 587 constants, growth-stage docs' capture-surface definition, the 588 claudinite-isolation carve-outs), the sheepdog pack's RULES.md (census 589 classification note — landed with this PR), and GCEC's `CLAUDE.md` / gcec 590 `RULES.md` routine pointers. 591 592 ## 11. Decisions on record (owner, 2026-07-22) 593 594 1. **Executor = per-repo CCR routine fired by the `ready-for-agent` label 595 event** (revised in review: event-wired, not an hourly poll). Keeps the 596 MCP-only session model, no repo secrets; per-task models via subagent 597 dispatch. 598 2. **Task layout = `tasks//` directory** per task (rename of `run_daily/`), 599 helpers beside `task.mjs`/`task.md`. 600 3. **Model field = family names** `opus | sonnet | haiku | none`, one vendored 601 family→id map. 602 4. **GCEC routines move into the gcec local pack** (`dev/routines/` folders 603 relocate; `routine.md` becomes `task.md`). 604 5. **`local_packs` → `local/packs`** (review): uniform pack depth, single scan 605 root; canonical declaration token `local/`, legacy forms accepted. 606 6. **The release workflow's independent cron is absorbed** into the 607 store-release task (review): the scheduler is the repo's only cron. 608 7. **Baselining (with migration-note apply folded in) is a per-repo basics 609 task**, not a fleet pass; migrations-retire stays canon-side with 610 stamp+probe evidence (review). 611 8. **Census and prose-to-checks are not fleet tasks** (review): the census is an 612 ordinary sheepdog pack task whose implementation happens to scan the fleet; 613 prose-to-checks is a canon-local task, **daily**. *(Prose-to-checks since 614 became a per-repo grow_with_claudinite task and moved to `weekly` — see the 615 as-built note in §6, table 2.)* 616 9. **Growth chain ordered across the four daily slots** (review): baselining + 617 migrations-apply `daily-2h` (02:00) → extract `daily-1h` (03:00) → promote 618 `daily` (04:00) → dedup `daily+1h` (05:00). *(Dedup since moved to `weekly`, 619 #582 — see the as-built note in §2; the rest of the chain is unchanged.)* 620 10. **Scheduler cron minute constrained to :10–:50** (review). 621
