1	// grow_with_claudinite task: usage-fold — the per-repo skill-usage aggregate
2	// (skill-usage-metrics DESIGN §5). `agent_model: 'none'` with
3	// `agent_preprocessing: 'node worker.mjs'`: the whole pass is deterministic code the
4	// scheduler runs as a subprocess — no agent, no dispatch issue, seconds of runtime.
5	//
6	// WHY: a skill is MOUNTED per repo, but mounting only puts a name and a one-line
7	// description into the session prompt — actually LOADING it is model discretion, and
8	// nothing recorded whether it ever happened. The only evidence is the session
9	// transcript, which is ephemeral and dies at retention on the logs branch. So the
10	// promotion ladder's skill-vs-prose call had no empirical feedback: a skill whose
11	// trigger never fires looked exactly like one that fires daily. This task counts
12	// loads — and the DENOMINATORS that make a count mean something — out of the logs
13	// this repo already captures, into a small tracked aggregate.
14	//
15	// It also counts what the SCHEDULER did: per task, how many runs dispatched an agent,
16	// how many were deterministic preprocessing only, how many its precondition skipped,
17	// how many failed, how many were deferred. Those come from the scheduler's own run
18	// records in its Actions logs — a census of scheduled work, beside the sample of
19	// captured sessions everything else here is drawn from.
20	//
21	// Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export.
22	
23	export default {
24	  id: 'usage-fold',
25	  frequency: 'daily',                    // day rows are the unit; a day closes once
26	  precondition_signals: ['conversationLogs'],
27	  agent_model: 'none',                   // pure code — no agent (agent-preprocessing DESIGN §4)
28	  expected_outcome: 'merged-pr',         // the regenerated GENERATED aggregate rides an auto-merging PR
29	  agent_preprocessing: 'node worker.mjs',
30	  // One tree read plus one blob read per capture file in the ~10-day window, all
31	  // local git, then one PR. A busy repo captures a few files a day, so this is
32	  // seconds; 600s is ~100x that, generous enough that a huge backlog on a first fold
33	  // still completes while a hung run is killed well inside the hourly cadence.
34	  agent_preprocessing_timeout: 600,
35	
36	  // Always runs. Deliberately NOT gated on fresh captures, nor on the logs branch
37	  // existing at all: the fold has two sources, and the second one — the scheduler's
38	  // own task-run records — exists in any repo that has a scheduler, including one
39	  // whose sessions are all unattended and captured nothing. Its job also includes
40	  // advancing the week watermark past days that have closed, which is true on a
41	  // quiet repo too. A run with nothing new recomputes to a byte-identical file and
42	  // opens no PR, so a wasted run costs seconds and produces no noise.
43	  precondition(signals) {
44	    const logs = signals.conversationLogs ?? {};
45	    const captured = logs.present === true
46	      ? `${logs.logCount ?? 0} captured log(s)`
47	      : 'no conversation-logs branch yet (task-run records only)';
48	    return { run: true, reason: `fold ${captured} into the usage aggregate (day rows recomputed, closed days folded into their week)` };
49	  },
50	};

- task id, pack, agent_model, has preprocessing?, uses CLAUDINITE_REQUEST_AGENT?
- VERDICT: adheres / violates / borderline
- Exact quotes (file:line) of any later-stage skip language: instructions in task.md telling the agent to verify preconditions, skip if no work, stop early if state changed; worker code exiting without doing work for non-error reasons other than "the work turned out to be empty".

1	// What each scheduler run DID to each due task, as one machine-readable line per
2	// evaluation in the run's Actions log (skill-usage-metrics DESIGN §4.2).
3	//
4	// WHY A LINE AND NOT A FILE. The scheduler is stateless by design — its only
5	// watermark is the Actions run ledger — and a per-run write to a tracked branch
6	// would be 24 commits a day of data the run already emits. The Actions log is the
7	// record the run already leaves, is retained by the platform, and is readable over
8	// one API call; so the run states its outcomes there and whatever usage aggregation
9	// a repo declares reads them back. This module is the SINGLE source of truth for that
10	// format: the renderer the scheduler prints with and the parser a reader reads with
11	// sit next to each other, with a round-trip test pinning them together, because a
12	// format written in one place and re-guessed in another is exactly the drift this
13	// repo bans.
14	//
15	// WHY NOT THE HUMAN SUMMARY LINE (`renderSummary`). That line is written BEFORE the
16	// actions run and reports what was PLANNED — an agentful task whose preprocessing
17	// then requested no agent still reads as its dispatch decision there. These records
18	// are derived AFTER the loop, from the same record the loop mutated, so they report
19	// what actually happened. The human summary stays what it is: prose for a person
20	// reading the run.
21	//
22	// The counts these produce are exact within the Actions log retention window, and
23	// that is worth stating next to the capture-derived counts they land beside: every
24	// scheduler run logs every due task, so a task's invocation counts are a CENSUS of
25	// scheduled work — unlike the skill and check counts, which see only the sessions
26	// that captured.
27	
28	// The five things a scheduler run can do with a due task. One name per outcome,
29	// used verbatim as the counter key in the aggregate, so there is no mapping table
30	// between "what the run said" and "what the fold counted" to drift.
31	export const TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES = Object.freeze([
32	  // A dispatch issue was filed: an executor session runs this task with an agent.
33	  'agent',
34	  // The task ran with NO agent — an `agent_model: none` task (preprocessing is the
35	  // whole task), or an agentful one whose preprocessing requested no agent stage.
36	  'preprocess',
37	  // Due, but its precondition said there was nothing to do.
38	  'skipped',
39	  // Its preprocessing failed; the run converged the task to a needs-human issue.
40	  'failed',
41	  // Due and past its precondition, but no NEW agent run started: this slot was
42	  // already dispatched (exactly-once), an earlier dispatch is still open
43	  // (at-most-one-open), or another task claimed the run exclusively. Work that
44	  // was wanted and did not happen this run.
45	  'deferred',
46	]);
47	
48	// An empty per-task counter row — every outcome present, zeros included, so a row's
49	// shape never depends on which outcomes a task happened to hit.
50	export const emptyTaskRun = () => Object.fromEntries(TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.map((o) => [o, 0]));
51	
52	// What this run did to one evaluated task, from the record the action loop left
53	// behind (`planRun`'s evaluation, mutated in `main`). Pure — every field it reads
54	// is already on the record.
55	export function taskRunOutcome(rec) {
56	  if (!rec.run) return 'skipped';
57	  // Another task claimed the run exclusively (planRun). Its precondition DID ask
58	  // for work, so this is not a skip — it is the deferred kind: wanted, not done.
59	  // Stated ahead of the shape checks below because a deferred record carries none
60	  // of the flags they read, and "no dispatch" would otherwise have to mean this by
61	  // accident rather than on purpose.
62	  if (rec.deferred) return 'deferred';
63	  if (rec.preprocessResult && !rec.preprocessResult.ok) return 'failed';
64	  if (rec.inline) return 'preprocess';
65	  // Agentful. With preprocessing, the agent stage is CONDITIONAL: a task that
66	  // absorbed its work into the deterministic pass stays quiet, and that is a run of
67	  // the task, not a skip of it.
68	  if (rec.preprocessing && !rec.agentRequested) return 'preprocess';
69	  return rec.dispatch?.action === 'create' ? 'agent' : 'deferred';
70	}
71	
72	// The line format. `v1` is the shape's version: a reader that meets a `v2` line
73	// knows it is looking at something it was not written for, instead of silently
74	// half-parsing it.
75	export const TASK_RUN_TAG = 'claudinite-task-run';
76	const VERSION = 'v1';
77	
78	export const renderTaskRun = (rec) =>
79	  `${TASK_RUN_TAG} ${VERSION} ${rec.pack}/${rec.task} [${rec.slotId}] ${taskRunOutcome(rec)}`;
80	
81	export const renderTaskRuns = (evaluations) => evaluations.map(renderTaskRun).join('\n');
82	
83	// Actions stamps every log line with its own timestamp before the command's output,
84	// so the parse tolerates that prefix — without it, a fetched log reads as having
85	// printed nothing at all.
86	const LINE_RE = new RegExp(
87	  String.raw`^(?:\S+\s+)?${TASK_RUN_TAG} ${VERSION} (\S+)/(\S+) \[(\S+)\] ([a-z-]+)\s*$`,
88	);
89	
90	// One line → `{ pack, task, slotId, outcome }`, or null for anything that is not a
91	// record of this version. Deliberately strict: an unknown outcome word is NOT a
92	// record, because counting it would mint a counter key nothing ever reads.
93	export function parseTaskRun(line) {
94	  const m = LINE_RE.exec(line);
95	  if (!m) return null;
96	  const [, pack, task, slotId, outcome] = m;
97	  if (!TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.includes(outcome)) return null;
98	  return { pack, task, slotId, outcome };
99	}
100	
101	// Every record in one job log. The log is the whole job's output — this picks its
102	// own lines out of it and ignores everything else.
103	export function parseTaskRuns(text) {
104	  const out = [];
105	  for (const line of String(text ?? '').split('\n')) {
106	    const rec = parseTaskRun(line);
107	    if (rec) out.push(rec);
108	  }
109	  return out;
110	}

1	# Skill-usage metrics — design
2	
3	Status: **agreed** (owner decisions recorded in §10; design review in the
4	2026-07-28 session). Refs #520. This document describes the **final state**
5	only; there is no migration plan — the rollout self-converges through the
6	existing machinery (the nightly vendored-canon refresh carries the code, a
7	baselining-applied migration note registers the hook), and the one ordering
8	constraint (§3.5) is satisfied by shipping the capture changes in one PR.
9	
10	The problem: skills are mounted per repo, but mounting only puts a name and a
11	one-line description into the session's system prompt — actually *loading* the
12	skill is model discretion, and nothing records whether it ever happens. The
13	only evidence is the session transcript, which is ephemeral (and, once captured
14	to the `conversation-logs` branch, deleted at retention). So the promotion
15	ladder's rung-4/rung-5 call — skill vs prose — has no empirical feedback: a
16	skill whose trigger never fires is indistinguishable from one that fires daily,
17	and a "skill" that fires in every session (rules wearing a skill's clothes) is
18	indistinguishable from a genuinely activity-scoped one.
19	
20	The same blind spot covers the **conformance checks**, from the other side. A
21	check that fails is a win: the finding reaches the session through the Stop
22	hook and the agent corrects before the work leaves the branch. Nothing counts
23	those corrections either — so "is this rule earning its place" and "is
24	enforcement even running" are as unanswerable as "does this skill ever load".
25	The checks ride the same pipeline, and §4.1 is where they are counted.
26	
27	A third blind spot sits outside sessions entirely. Most of what a repo does on a
28	schedule opens no session at all — a precondition that finds nothing to do, an
29	`agent_model: none` task whose deterministic pass is the whole task, a dispatch
30	suppressed because an earlier one is still open — so "how much agent work did
31	this task cause" and "is this task doing anything" are not under-counted by the
32	capture pipeline, they are absent from it. §4.2 counts them from the scheduler's
33	own run records. And the sessions that *do* run unattended never captured at all
34	until §3.4: an executor session ends by having its container reclaimed, which is
35	exactly the ending no `SessionEnd` hook fires on.
36	
37	The shape: session transcripts already record every skill invocation, and the
38	check runners leave readable marks in them too. Capture already ships
39	transcripts to each repo's orphan `conversation-logs` branch at merge time.
40	This design (a) enriches capture with a best-effort session-end event and an
41	explicit one for unattended runs, (b) adds a deterministic daily **fold** in each
42	repo that counts skill loads, check activations and failures, activity
43	denominators, and task invocations into a small tracked aggregate, and (c) adds a
44	**fleet sweep** in the sheepdog pack that recomputes a fleet-wide aggregate from
45	the members' files into the fleet-enforcer repo. Every stage is deterministic
46	code — no agent judgment anywhere in the pipeline.
47	
48	```
49	transcript ──(merge capture / SessionEnd capture / the executor's own last step)──▶ conversation-logs branch
50	    conversation-logs ─────┐
51	    scheduler run logs ────┴──(usage-fold, per repo, daily)──▶ .claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json
52	    member usage files ───────(fleet-usage, sheepdog, daily)──▶ usage-fleet.GENERATED.json (enforcer repo)
53	```
54	
55	---
56	
57	## 1. Where knowledge lives — the placement rule
58	
59	The canon knows **mechanisms**, never repos. The fleet-enforcer repo knows
60	**the fleet**. Each member knows **itself**.
61	
62	| piece | home | knows about |
63	|---|---|---|
64	| capture (merge + SessionEnd + the executor's explicit call) | `grow_with_claudinite` pack (canon) | its own session, its own logs branch |
65	| the task-run record format | `engine/scheduler/run-record.mjs` (core) | the scheduler's own outcomes — no pack, no repo |
66	| `usage-fold` (daily) | `grow_with_claudinite/tasks/usage-fold/` (canon) | its own logs branch, its own aggregate file |
67	| `fleet-usage` (daily) | `sheepdog/tasks/fleet-usage/` (canon pack; runs only where sheepdog is declared) | nothing hardcoded — members enumerated at runtime from the sheepdog config (`{ owner, kind, exclude, canonRepo }`) via `fleet-api.mjs`, exactly as `fleet-census` does |
68	| the fleet aggregate | the fleet-enforcer repo's default branch | — |
69	
70	No repo list exists in any code, canon or otherwise. The member set is derived
71	where it already is today for the census and freshness sweeps.
72	
73	## 2. Sources of truth, and what is derived
74	
75	- The **transcript** is the source of truth for what happened in a session.
76	- The **`conversation-logs` branch** is a byte-faithful (scrubbed) window onto
77	  transcripts, retained `retention_days` (§3).
78	- The **scheduler's Actions log** is the source of truth for what each run did
79	  with each due task, by an owned contract rather than by scraping (§4.2).
80	- The **per-repo aggregate** is derived: capture-derived day rows are a pure
81	  function of the live logs; task rows are appended once past their own run
82	  watermark; week rows are append-once sums of closed day rows (§5).
83	- The **fleet aggregate** is derived: a pure function of the current member
84	  files, fully recomputed each run (§6). Never store what you can derive —
85	  the fleet file keeps full (week × repo × skill) grain precisely so every
86	  coarser view remains derivable from it.
87	
88	Both aggregate files are `GENERATED`-named and machine-written only, under the
89	canon's GENERATED-file discipline (regenerated, never hand-edited).
90	
91	## 3. Capture — three events, one idempotent mechanism
92	
93	### 3.1 The delta contract (existing, now pinned by tests)
94	
95	`capture-log.mjs` keys on the **session id**: every capture refetches the
96	branch tip, finds all prior `*--<sessionId>.jsonl` files (whatever event or
97	issue produced them), takes the max entry timestamp across them, and pushes
98	only the entries strictly after it. Zero delta ⇒ no file, no commit, no push.
99	This makes double-writing safe **by construction** — any two capture events for
100	one session chain into disjoint files — and it is the property the SessionEnd
101	hook (§3.3) relies on, so it is pinned by dedicated tests (repeat capture of an
102	unchanged transcript produces nothing; a post-merge tail produces exactly the
103	tail).
104	
105	One file therefore maps 1:1 to a **capture event**, not to a merge.
106	
107	### 3.2 No-issue captures: `issue-0`
108	
109	The filename stays `<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`, with **`0` meaning
110	"no associated issue"**. The filename regex, the retention prune, and the
111	scheduler's `conversationLogs` signal already accept `0` — only the CLI's
112	argument validation refuses it, and that is the whole change. Keeping the
113	filename shape identical is deliberate: any *new* shape would be invisible to
114	the prune and become immortal. The extract's conversation half treats an
115	`issue-0` file as having no issue to post its exchange summary on; everything
116	else about its two-pass lifecycle is unchanged.
117	
118	### 3.3 The SessionEnd hook — best effort, fail-soft
119	
120	A `SessionEnd` hook (`engine/hooks/session-end-command.mjs`, registered in the
121	consumer's `.claude/settings.json` like its siblings) runs capture with
122	`--issue 0`. Properties:
123	
124	- **SessionEnd, not Stop.** Stop fires at every turn end (and already runs the
125	  conformance checks); capturing there would push to the orphan branch once per
126	  turn and shred the branch into per-turn files. SessionEnd fires once.
127	- **Best effort, and that is enough.** A container reclaimed by timeout never
128	  fires it. Every firing strictly enriches the record (non-merging sessions,
129	  and the post-merge tail of merging ones); every miss leaves exactly today's
130	  behaviour. No correctness anywhere depends on the hook having fired.
131	- **Fail-soft.** It swallows every error, logs the attempt via `hooklog`, and
132	  must never block a session from ending. Absent `grow_with_claudinite` in the
133	  repo's declared packs, it exits without acting.
134	- Scrubbing is the existing capture scrub, unchanged — the hook adds a capture
135	  *event*, not a new write path.
136	
137	### 3.4 The unattended sessions — capture where no hook fires
138	
139	The two events above cover the sessions a **human** is in. They covered none of
140	the sessions a human is not: a scheduled task's executor session runs a dispatch
141	in a cloud container, never merges through `merge-to-main` (its task delivers by
142	opening a PR, or by converging its issue), and ends by having that container
143	reclaimed — which is exactly the ending that fires no `SessionEnd`. Measured on
144	the canon repo the day this was written: **47 capture files, not one of them from
145	an executor session**, while the scheduler had dispatched hundreds. Every skill
146	those runs loaded and every check that caught something in them was invisible.
147	
148	The fix is not a third capture path but the **same** step, invoked deliberately
149	instead of waited for. `session-end-command.mjs` is a runner, not a hook body: it
150	invokes every active pack's `session-end.mjs`, discovering them structurally. So
151	the executor's last step (`executor.md` step 5, after its issue is converged)
152	runs that runner itself:
153	
154	```bash
155	CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE=<issue> node <engine>/hooks/session-end-command.mjs
156	```
157	
158	- **`CLAUDINITE_SESSION_ISSUE`** is the runner's documented pass-through: *the
159	  issue this session was about, when its launcher knew one*. A hook firing never
160	  does (nothing tells `SessionEnd` what the session was for), so it is only ever
161	  set by an explicit invocation. The capture step uses it in place of `0` — which
162	  files an unattended run's log under **the dispatch issue whose title names
163	  `pack/task`**, so the log is attributable to the task that produced it rather
164	  than landing in the issueless pile.
165	- **Core still names no pack.** The executor invokes a runner; the runner invokes
166	  whatever steps the declared packs contribute; a repo that declares no capturing
167	  pack does nothing at all.
168	- **Mid-session invocation is safe and lossy in one known way**: the transcript is
169	  complete only up to that call, so the executor's own final message is not in the
170	  file. If the hook *does* fire later, its capture is a second event over the same
171	  session, which §3.1's session-keyed delta already makes safe by construction.
172	- **It cannot fail the dispatch.** The issue is already converged; a failed
173	  capture is reported in the session's final message and nothing else.
174	
175	The one thing this cannot assert in advance is whether a *trigger-started*
176	session can push to the logs branch at all. Capture pushes over `origin` with
177	git, not over the MCP GitHub tools the executor is otherwise restricted to; every
178	existing capture on the branch was pushed from a cloud container of the same
179	kind, but all of them were owner-started sessions. If a trigger-started one turns
180	out to lack that credential, the step reports the failure in the session's final
181	message and the outcome is exactly today's — no capture, nothing worse — and the
182	task-invocation counts (§4.2) are unaffected, because they never depended on a
183	session at all.
184	
185	### 3.5 Ordering constraint
186	
187	The idempotence tests and the `issue-0` relaxation must be in the canon before
188	the hook registration reaches any member — an old `conversation-extract` would
189	try to comment on issue `#0`. Shipping all of §3 in one canon PR satisfies
190	this; the baselining task refreshes a member's mount before applying migration
191	notes, so a member can never run the hook against a stale capture script.
192	
193	## 4. Counting — one tested function per question
194	
195	All counting happens in the fold worker (§5), in exported, individually tested
196	functions. The capture path computes nothing.
197	
198	- **`skillLoads`** (per skill name): `Skill` tool_use entries, plus user-typed
199	  `/command` entries whose name matches a skill mounted in this repo (the
200	  mounted set comes from the pack registry — `loadPacks()` — not from the
201	  gitignored `.claude/skills/` mounts). Built-in CLI commands (`/model`,
202	  `/clear`, …) never match. Sidechain (subagent) streams are included — a
203	  subagent loading a skill is a load.
204	- **`captures`**: files folded (capture events). **`merges`**: the subset with
205	  issue > 0. Once the SessionEnd hook exists, these differ — the split exists
206	  from day one so no consumer ever reads an ambiguous column.
207	- **`sessions`**: distinct session ids among the bucket's captures (one
208	  session can capture more than once).
209	- **`userMessages`**: genuine human turns — user-role entries that are neither
210	  tool results nor scheduled-task/automated firings (the transcript marks
211	  these). This heuristic is the most fragile line in the design, so it lives
212	  in one function with fixtures for each entry shape it excludes.
213	- **`userCommands`**: user-typed `/command` entries, all of them — the
214	  cleanest "explicit asks" workload measure.
215	
216	Stated overlap: a typed `/merge-to-main` counts in both `userCommands` and
217	`skillLoads` — one event, two axes, both true.
218	
219	### 4.1 Check activations — and, above all, check *failures*
220	
221	Skills are half the picture. The conformance checks are the other half, and the
222	more valuable half: a check that **fails is a win**. The finding lands back in
223	the session through the Stop hook and the agent corrects before the work
224	leaves the branch — so "how often did the checks catch something" is a direct
225	measure of what the corpus is worth, and "which rule caught it" is the most
226	actionable number in the whole pipeline.
227	
228	Neither runner writes a metrics file, so both are counted off the marks they
229	already leave in the transcript. There are exactly three, each verified against
230	real captured logs rather than inferred:
231	
232	1. **The Stop hook's `hooklog` line** — `<iso> run=<id> Stop: done exit=<n>
233	   <reason>`. It reaches the transcript because `hooklog` mirrors to stderr and
234	   the harness records hook stderr (as an `isMeta` feedback turn, a
235	   `stop_hook_summary`, or a `hook_success` attachment). This is the **only**
236	   mark a *passing* run leaves, which is what makes work-scope run counts — not
237	   merely failure counts — possible at all. Its `reason` distinguishes the four
238	   outcomes the hook itself declares: `checks-passed`, `blocking-findings`,
239	   `loop-guard-relent` (blocking findings that survived two fix attempts — a
240	   failure that prints no findings block, readable *only* here), and
241	   `runner-error` (the checks did not run, an anti-win that would otherwise
242	   masquerade as a quiet clean day).
243	2. **`report-findings`' summary line** — `N blocking, M advisory (<scope>
244	   scope: …)`. It names its own scope and survives the `| tail` an agent
245	   usually pipes a run through. It is printed *only* when there were findings,
246	   so it counts failures and finding volume — never runs.
247	3. **The runner's invocation in a Bash command** (`node …/check_the_world.mjs`).
248	   This is how the world scope runs at all: its Stop-hook sibling does not
249	   exist, because the world sweep is wired into the test/CI flow rather than
250	   the hook (`engine/checks/README.md`, "Enforcement wiring").
251	
252	**CI counts when the agent was in the loop on it.** Write, commit, let CI run,
253	fix what it caught is the same correction loop as the Stop hook's, one turn
254	wider, so a CI check failure the session acted on is the same kind of win. It
255	is counted exactly when the session **pulled the job log in** — which is what
256	"the agent was in the loop" means operationally, and it draws the line the
257	owner asked for: a nightly or post-merge run nobody looked at stays uncounted,
258	correctly, because nothing was corrected. Two things follow, and both are
259	mechanism, not policy:
260	
261	- CI logs arrive through a CI-log tool rather than Bash (matched by name shape
262	  — `job_logs` / `run_logs` / `workflow_logs` — so a different MCP server or a
263	  rename still lands), and every line carries the Actions timestamp in front of
264	  the command's own output, so each mark tolerates that prefix. Without it a
265	  fetched CI log reads as having printed nothing.
266	- A job log can be fetched repeatedly while iterating on the failure, and
267	  nothing in a fetch says *which run* it was. So CI texts dedupe on the check
268	  output itself: two fetches of one job are identical and collapse; two real
269	  runs differ by their Actions timestamps at least. Two genuinely identical
270	  runs collapse too — an under-count, the direction this counter is allowed to
271	  be wrong in.
272	
273	From those, per bucket:
274	
275	- **`checks`**, keyed by scope (`work` / `world`): `runs` — observed
276	  activations; `failures` — the subset that reported at least one blocking
277	  finding; `errors` — runs where the runner could not launch; `blocking` /
278	  `advisory` — finding *volume* summed over those runs. A rule blocking in two
279	  consecutive runs counts twice: the question is how often the checks caught
280	  something, not how many distinct problems existed. Plus `ciRuns` /
281	  `ciFailures`, the **subset** of those that came from a fetched CI log —
282	  carried separately because that source can only see a run that printed
283	  something (a green CI sweep prints nothing and is invisible), so a consumer
284	  wanting a rate over runs it can see the whole of subtracts them, while one
285	  asking "how often did the checks catch something" uses the totals.
286	- **`checkFindings`**, keyed by rule id, `{ blocking, advisory }` — read off
287	  each rendered `[BLOCKING] <rule>  <file>` header. Lossier than the summary
288	  totals (a run piped through `tail -3` keeps the summary and drops the
289	  headers), which is why both are kept: a gap between them *is* the truncation,
290	  visible rather than assumed away.
291	
292	Runs are counted only from the marks a passing run also leaves — hook
293	completion lines, and Bash invocations — never from the summary line. Where a
294	runner ran without its command naming it (a `make test` step wrapping it), the
295	summary lines in its output are the floor: the count is the **max** of the two
296	signals, never their sum, because they are two views of the same runs.
297	
298	Two things keep this honest and must stay stated wherever the numbers are read:
299	
300	- **Only Bash and CI-log tool results count**, paired back to their `tool_use`.
301	  In the corpus that owns the runners, reading a file that merely *contains*
302	  this vocabulary is the ordinary case, not a corner one.
303	- **These are floors, never over-counts.** A sweep whose CI log nobody fetched
304	  left no mark in any transcript. A hook killed before it logged left none
305	  either. A green CI run prints nothing to be seen by. The bias is
306	  one-directional by construction, which is the direction that keeps "the
307	  checks caught N things this week" a claim worth making.
308	
309	One hook execution is recorded under two entry shapes (the feedback turn the
310	model sees, and the harness's `stop_hook_summary` repeating the same stderr).
311	They dedupe on the `hooklog` stamps the text carries — the one identity stable
312	across both shapes and unique per execution. Counting both would double every
313	failure, which is precisely the number that must not be inflated.
314	
315	Zeros are implicit everywhere: a mounted skill with no loads simply has no
316	key. Consumers derive the zero set by diffing against the repo's mounted
317	skills (pack registry for a member; for the fleet view, each member's declared
318	packs), which is what makes "never loads" visible at all.
319	
320	### 4.2 Task invocations — what the scheduler did, from the scheduler's own log
321	
322	Skill loads and check failures are both read out of *sessions*. A whole half of
323	what a repo does never opens a session at all: a precondition that says "nothing
324	to do", an `agent_model: none` task whose deterministic pass is the entire task,
325	a dispatch suppressed because an earlier one is still open. None of those leave a
326	transcript, and the first of them is the single most common thing the scheduler
327	does. So "how much agent work did this task actually cause" and "is this task
328	doing anything at all" were unanswerable from the capture pipeline by
329	construction — not under-counted, absent.
330	
331	**Source: the scheduler's own Actions log, by contract rather than by scraping.**
332	Each run prints one machine-readable record per evaluated task —
333	`claudinite-task-run v1 <pack>/<task> [<slot>] <outcome>` — emitted **after** the
334	action loop, so it states what happened rather than what was planned. Renderer
335	and parser live in one module (`engine/scheduler/run-record.mjs`) with a
336	round-trip test, because a format written in one place and re-guessed in another
337	is precisely the drift this corpus bans. The human job-summary line is
338	deliberately *not* the source: it is written before the actions run, so an
339	agentful task whose preprocessing then requested no agent still reads there as
340	its dispatch decision.
341	
342	**Why a log line and not a file.** The scheduler is stateless by design — its
343	only watermark is the Actions run ledger — and a per-run write to a tracked
344	branch would be 24 commits a day of data the run already emits. Writing them to
345	the `conversation-logs` branch was considered and rejected for a second reason:
346	that branch's retention prune is *filename-shaped*, so a new shape on it would be
347	invisible to the prune and become immortal (§3.2).
348	
349	**The five outcomes**, one counter each, keyed by `pack/task`:
350	
351	| outcome | means |
352	|---|---|
353	| `agent` | a dispatch issue was filed — an executor session ran this task with an agent |
354	| `preprocess` | the task ran with no agent: `agent_model: none`, or an agentful task whose preprocessing requested no agent stage |
355	| `skipped` | due, but its precondition said there was nothing to do |
356	| `failed` | its preprocessing failed; the run converged it to a needs-human issue |
357	| `deferred` | due and past its precondition, but no new agent run started (this slot was already dispatched, or an earlier dispatch is still open) |
358	
359	`failed` and `deferred` are not decoration. Folding `failed` into `preprocess`
360	would make a task that fails every night identical to one that works every night;
361	folding `deferred` into `agent` would report executions that never happened, and
362	into `skipped` would hide a task whose dispatches are piling up unrun.
363	
364	**Forward-only, past a `runsFoldedThrough` watermark** — the one place the day
365	tier departs from "recomputed from scratch every run" (§5), and the reason is the
366	source rather than taste. The capture files are a local git branch the fold
367	re-reads for free; the run logs are a paged REST resource at two calls per run,
368	where re-reading a 10-day window nightly would cost ~20× the API calls for an
369	identical answer. So each fold reads only the completed runs newer than the
370	watermark, and the watermark is the whole exactly-once mechanism. It advances
371	past an idle run too — a quiet hour legitimately prints no records, and re-reading
372	it forever is the one way this stays expensive. The trade is the same one the
373	week rows already make and is stated the same way: **a counting bug fixed later
374	applies from the fix forward, it does not heal history.** A per-fold cap
375	(240 runs, ~10 days of catch-up) bounds a backlog, advances the watermark only
376	through what it actually read, and *logs the remainder* rather than truncating
377	silently.
378	
379	**These rows are a census, not a sample** — and that is the sharpest difference
380	between them and everything else in the file. Every scheduler run records every
381	due task, whether or not a session was ever captured. The distinction is stated
382	in the fleet file's own `_note`, because a consumer reading task counts beside
383	skill counts would otherwise apply the sampling caveat to both.
384	
385	**Fail-soft and independent.** An unreadable ledger costs the task rows for that
386	run and nothing else; the watermark stays put, so the next fold retries exactly
387	those runs.
388	
389	## 5. The per-repo aggregate — `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json`
390	
391	Written by **`usage-fold`**: an agentless daily task of `grow_with_claudinite`
392	(deterministic preprocessing, no agent, cheapest possible run), outcome
393	`merged-pr` — the worker opens a PR with the regenerated file and arms
394	auto-merge; a byte-identical recompute opens nothing. It lives under
395	`.claudinite/local/` because that is the repo-owned area the vendoring refresh
396	never touches — the mount root itself is read-only canon.
397	
398	Two tiers, per the owner's fast-insight requirement:
399	
400	- **Days** (short term): keyed by the capture filename's UTC date. A file's
401	  stamp is its push moment, so day *D* gains files only during *D* and is
402	  immutable once *D* ends. While a day is inside the raw retention window, the
403	  fold recomputes it **from scratch from the live files, every run** — no
404	  ingest ledger, no double-count risk, and a counting-bug fix self-heals the
405	  whole visible window on its next run. Day rows older than the window drop
406	  out of the file (their content lives on in their week row).
407	- **Weeks** (long term): ISO-8601 weeks, append-once via a single
408	  **`foldedThrough` watermark**. Each run, every completed day *d* with
409	  `foldedThrough < d < today` is added into its week and the mark advances.
410	  Days close strictly in order, so a monotone mark is the entire exactly-once
411	  mechanism. Days fold at day+1 — long before their raw files die — so the
412	  pipeline tolerates ~`retention_days − 1` consecutive days of task outage
413	  before losing anything; past that, the loss is **visible, never silent**:
414	  each week row records how many days it absorbed (`days: 5` declares its own
415	  hole).
416	
417	The task-invocation rows (§4.2) ride in the same two tiers and fold into weeks
418	identically, but reach the day tier by the other mechanism: appended once past
419	`runsFoldedThrough`, on top of what earlier folds counted, rather than
420	recomputed. They are accumulated **before** the week fold, so a day that closes
421	carries its scheduler counts into its week in the same pass that freezes it. Two
422	consequences worth stating rather than discovering: a day with scheduler activity
423	and no captures still gets a day row (a repo whose sessions are all unattended
424	would otherwise show nothing at all), and those rows leave the day tier on their
425	own 14-day window rather than the raw retention window, because nothing about
426	them ages out when a capture file does.
427	
428	The fold's precondition is therefore no longer "there is a `conversation-logs`
429	branch": it has two sources, and the second exists in any repo that has a
430	scheduler. A repo that has never captured folds its task rows and nothing else.
431	
432	```json
433	{
434	  "version": 1,
435	  "foldedThrough": "2026-07-26",
436	  "runsFoldedThrough": "2026-07-28T22:44:00Z",
437	  "days": {
438	    "2026-07-28": { "captures": 3, "merges": 2, "sessions": 2,
439	                    "userMessages": 31, "userCommands": 4,
440	                    "skillLoads": { "merge-to-main": 1 },
441	                    "tasks": { "tidy-repo/tidy-issues":
442	                                 { "agent": 1, "preprocess": 0, "skipped": 23,
443	                                   "failed": 0, "deferred": 0 } },
444	                    "checks": {
445	                      "work":  { "runs": 34, "failures": 12, "errors": 0, "blocking": 15,
446	                                 "advisory": 0, "ciRuns": 0, "ciFailures": 0 },
447	                      "world": { "runs": 42, "failures": 3, "errors": 0, "blocking": 5,
448	                                 "advisory": 131, "ciRuns": 1, "ciFailures": 1 }
449	                    },
450	                    "checkFindings": { "task-lifecycle": { "blocking": 8, "advisory": 0 } } }
451	  },
452	  "weeks": {
453	    "2026-W30": { "days": 7, "captures": 11, "merges": 9, "sessionDays": 8,
454	                  "userMessages": 210, "userCommands": 23,
455	                  "skillLoads": { "merge-to-main": 6 },
456	                  "tasks": { "tidy-repo/tidy-issues":
457	                               { "agent": 7, "preprocess": 0, "skipped": 161,
458	                                 "failed": 0, "deferred": 0 } },
459	                  "checks": { "work": { "runs": 190, "failures": 51, "errors": 0, "blocking": 66,
460	                                        "advisory": 3, "ciRuns": 0, "ciFailures": 0 } },
461	                  "checkFindings": { "task-lifecycle": { "blocking": 40, "advisory": 0 } } }
462	  }
463	}
464	```
465	
466	Keys are sorted for stable diffs. All counters sum exactly under folding —
467	except distinct-session counts, which do not (a session spanning two days is
468	distinct in each). Weeks therefore carry **`sessionDays`** — the sum of the
469	day-level distinct counts — named for what it is rather than pretending to a
470	precision folding cannot give.
471	
472	Frozen weeks are a stated trade, not a surprise: a counting bug found later
473	heals the day window automatically, but weeks folded under the old counting
474	keep it — re-freezing would need raw data the retention TTL deliberately
475	destroyed. Git history records which commit folded what, so the boundary is
476	auditable. The same trade applies to a *new* counter: weeks folded before the
477	check counts existed carry no `checks` key, and the fold extends them from the
478	day they close forward rather than refusing to advance the watermark past them
479	— a partial series beats a wedged one, and the boundary is visible in the file.
480	
481	Precondition: none — it runs daily. Runs where nothing changed are no-ops (no
482	PR), and the agentless run costs seconds.
483	
484	## 6. The fleet aggregate — `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json`
485	
486	Written by **`fleet-usage`**: an agentless daily task of the **sheepdog**
487	pack, alongside `fleet-census` and `fleet-freshness` and shaped exactly like
488	them — the sweep (`aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs`, inside the task's folder) *is*
489	the `agent_preprocessing`, `required_secrets` asks for `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`,
490	and members are enumerated via `fleet-api.mjs` from the sheepdog config entry.
491	It runs only where the sheepdog pack is declared — the fleet-enforcer repo.
492	
493	The aggregation is a **stateless full recompute**: read each member's
494	`.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` at its default branch over REST (one
495	file per member, no clones), and rebuild the fleet file as a pure function of
496	the inputs. Stateless recompute is idempotent by definition and self-heals any
497	past error; at this cardinality (~repos × skills × weeks, all small) there is
498	nothing to optimize.
499	
500	- **Grain**: full (week × repo × skill, week × repo × **rule**, and week × repo
501	  × **task**) for history, plus the members' current day windows verbatim for the fast view —
502	  "what happened this week?" at day-grain, trends at week-grain. Nothing
503	  pre-summed. The checks are carried at the same grain and for the same reason
504	  as the skill loads: whether a rule earns its place is a fleet-shaped
505	  question. A rule that never fires in one repo may simply not be that repo's
506	  subject; a rule that never fires in **any** of them is mis-described or
507	  worthless — and a rule that keeps firing everywhere is the corpus's
508	  best-performing guard. Only a view across every member tells those apart.
509	- **Coverage is explicit**: a member without the usage file (not yet folding)
510	  or with an unreadable one is listed in a `coverage` section as absent —
511	  census-style, never silently skipped — so gaps in the denominators are
512	  visible rather than baked in. A member still on an older fold (no `checks`
513	  key) lands as an empty check row rather than an exception: the sweep leads
514	  the members' upgrades, so that is the normal state for a while.
515	- **A `_note` field** states the sampling population: captured sessions only —
516	  merging sessions plus sessions that ended cleanly enough for the SessionEnd
517	  hook. Reclaimed containers and crashes are invisible. The file must not read
518	  as a census. The note carries the checks' second, narrower boundary too: the
519	  counts are what a *session* saw, so a world sweep that ran in CI is not in
520	  them, and every check number is a floor on activations.
521	- Outcome `merged-pr` (owner decision): the sweep opens a PR on a run-stamped
522	  branch in the enforcer repo and arms auto-merge. This keeps the write inside
523	  the outcome taxonomy `verify-outcome.mjs` enforces, lets the enforcer's CI
524	  gate a malformed file, and makes the daily PR stream a browsable audit trail.
525	  A byte-identical recompute opens nothing.
526	
527	## 7. Consumers — who learns from this
528	
529	- **The owner**, ad hoc: both files are small sorted JSON on tracked branches —
530	  readable in the GitHub UI, over MCP, or via `git show`, with full history.
531	- **Canon curation** (the promote run): the empirical feedback the rung-4/5
532	  routing decision currently lacks, in both directions. Never loads across the
533	  fleet ⇒ the trigger is mis-described, or the content should not be gated at
534	  all (rules wearing a skill's clothes); always loads ⇒ likewise not
535	  activity-scoped. Raw counts alone cannot distinguish healthy-rare from
536	  broken — a version-bump skill loading rarely is fine — which is why the
537	  denominators exist: the metric is loads against the sessions where the
538	  skill's own declared trigger plausibly applied.
539	- **Canon curation, on the rules** (the same run): the checks' half answers a
540	  sharper question than the skills' half, because a check failure is an
541	  observed correction rather than an inferred one. A rule with steady failures
542	  across the fleet is a guard earning its keep and an argument for converting
543	  more prose into checks (`prose-to-checks`); a rule that has never fired
544	  anywhere is either unreachable or describing something that does not happen;
545	  a rule firing on nearly every run is a *default the corpus should change*
546	  rather than a violation worth blocking on. `errors` reads differently from
547	  all three: it means enforcement was silently off, and it is the one number
548	  here whose right value is zero.
549	- **The scheduled system itself** (new with §4.2): whether a task earns its slot
550	  is now answerable. A task that has skipped every run in every member for weeks
551	  has a precondition that never fires — either its signal is broken or the work
552	  it waits for does not happen. One with a steady `failed` count is broken
553	  machinery rather than a bad night. One with a rising `deferred` count is
554	  dispatching faster than its executor drains. And "how many agent executions did
555	  this task cause" — the cost question — has a number instead of an impression.
556	- **Sheepdog's fleet tasks**, later: freshness-style drift issues citing the
557	  fleet file ("skill X: 0 loads fleet-wide in 6 weeks"). The learning loop
558	  stays in the enforcer's domain, not the canon's. Out of scope here; noted so
559	  the file's grain is chosen for it (it is).
560	
561	## 8. TTLs, end to end
562	
563	| data | where | TTL |
564	|---|---|---|
565	| transcript | harness config dir | harness-owned (ephemeral in cloud sessions) |
566	| raw capture `.jsonl` | `conversation-logs` branch | `retention_days` (unchanged; unset ⇒ capture-only, no prune) |
567	| scheduler run log | GitHub Actions | platform-owned (90 days by default) |
568	| day rows (capture-derived) | member usage file | the raw window — then their week row carries them |
569	| day rows (task invocations) | member usage file | 14 days — then their week row carries them |
570	| week rows | member usage file | indefinite (~KBs/year; revisit only if a file nears 1 MB) |
571	| fleet file | enforcer repo | none needed — derived; history is git's |
572	
573	## 9. Failure modes, stated
574	
575	- **Fold outage** longer than ~`retention_days − 1` days: unfolded days lose
576	  their raw backing. The hole is visible (week's `days` count short), never a
577	  silently wrong number.
578	- **Hook never fires** (reclaim, crash): the record degrades exactly to
579	  today's merge-only capture. No consumer breaks. For an *unattended* session
580	  that is the normal case, which is why its capture is an explicit step rather
581	  than a hook (§3.4); if that step is skipped or fails, that session is
582	  invisible exactly as it was before, and its task-invocation record (§4.2) is
583	  unaffected — the scheduler logged it either way.
584	- **Scrub boundary** (unchanged from capture's existing statement): a secret
585	  the session itself transformed is invisible to any static scrub; the branch
586	  shares the repo's access control and push protection stays the last net.
587	- **A member goes quiet**: its day window empties, its weeks stop growing, and
588	  the fleet file shows it with zeros-by-absence plus its last folded week —
589	  distinguishable from "not folding" via the `coverage` section.
590	- **A check ran where no session saw it** (a CI run nobody fetched the log for,
591	  a hook killed before it logged, a green CI sweep that printed nothing): the
592	  run is simply not counted. This is the one under-count the design accepts by
593	  construction, and it is one-directional — the numbers are floors, never
594	  inflated. Stated in the fleet file's own `_note` so a consumer cannot read
595	  them as a census of enforcement. Detached CI is *deliberately* out: the
596	  metric is about the correction loop, and a run nobody looked at corrected
597	  nothing.
598	- **Fold outage longer than the Actions log retention**: the task records for
599	  those runs are gone, and the watermark still points before them, so the fold
600	  reads what survives and the lost runs are simply never counted. Silent in the
601	  file itself — but the same outage is loud in the week rows' `days` count, and
602	  the fold would have to be down for ~90 days for it to happen at all.
603	- **A run's log is unreadable** (a 404, a rate limit): the task rows do not
604	  advance that run, the watermark stays put, and the next fold retries exactly
605	  those runs. The skill and check counts are unaffected — the two sources fail
606	  independently, by design.
607	- **A counting bug in the task rows**: unlike the capture-derived days, these do
608	  NOT self-heal, because the fold no longer re-reads the runs behind them. A fix
609	  applies from the fix forward. This is the price of not re-fetching a
610	  rate-limited API every night, and it is the same trade the week rows make.
611	- **The harness changes how it records hooks**: the marks in §4.1 are harness
612	  output, not a contract Claudinite owns. A shape change makes check counts
613	  fall to zero — loudly, since a repo with checks wired cannot plausibly report
614	  no activations — rather than drift quietly wrong. Each mark is read by one
615	  exported function with a fixture copied from a real capture, so re-pinning is
616	  a fixture update, not an investigation.
617	
618	## 10. Decisions on record (owner, 2026-07-28)
619	
620	1. **Two tiers, days + weeks** — days for insight faster than a week, matched
621	   to the 10-day raw TTL; weeks as the long-term series, aggregated from days.
622	2. **Days statelessly recomputed; weeks append-once from days** — the
623	   watermark replaces any ingest ledger.
624	3. **Denominators include sessions and user commands**, alongside captures,
625	   merges, and user messages.
626	4. **Fleet awareness is the sheepdog domain** — the canon must not know
627	   specific member repos; the aggregate lands in the fleet-enforcer repo via
628	   its pack's tasks.
629	5. **Auto-merged daily PR, not a direct commit**, for the GENERATED aggregate
630	   writes — into the enforcer repo, and by extension the member fold.
631	6. **SessionEnd capture is a welcome best-effort bonus**, contingent on
632	   double-write safety being proven first (§3.1's tests), with `issue-0`
633	   naming for issueless captures.
634	7. **No migration plan** — the existing convergence machinery carries the
635	   rollout; ordering is handled by shipping §3 in one PR (§3.5).
636	
637	### Owner, 2026-07-29
638	
639	8. **Check activations and check failures are counted too** (§4.1), at both
640	   levels — per repo in the fold, and fleet-wide in the sheepdog sweep, exactly
641	   as the skill loads are. **Failures are the point**: when a check fails the
642	   agent corrects immediately, so a failure is a win, and every one is counted.
643	   Executions are counted as far as the transcript allows and the shortfall is
644	   stated rather than papered over (§9) — the numbers are floors.
645	9. **Per-rule grain is kept**, not just per-scope totals: "which rule catches
646	   things" is what the promote run and `prose-to-checks` actually need, and it
647	   is what the fleet view exists to answer across members.
648	10. **CI counts when it was part of the agent loop** — write, commit, let CI
649	    run, fix what it caught — and not otherwise. Operationally: the session
650	    pulled the job log in. A nightly or post-merge run nobody looked at is
651	    explicitly *not crucial* and stays uncounted, because nothing was
652	    corrected. The CI share is carried separately (`ciRuns` / `ciFailures`)
653	    since that source sees only runs that printed.
654	
655	### Owner, 2026-07-29 (second round)
656	
657	11. **Unattended runs must reach the conversation-logs branch** (§3.4). They did
658	    not: no executor session had ever been captured, because those sessions end
659	    by container reclaim and merge nothing. Capture becomes an explicit last step
660	    of the executor routine, filed under its dispatch issue, rather than a hook
661	    firing nobody can rely on.
662	12. **The aggregation counts task invocations** (§4.2), per task: agent
663	    executions first, and beside them the runs that were deterministic
664	    preprocessing only and the runs whose precondition said no. Read from the
665	    Actions logs — all task invocation data is already there — which keeps the
666	    scheduler stateless and needs no new storage anywhere.
667	13. **`failed` and `deferred` are counted too**, not folded into their
668	    neighbours: a task that fails every night must not read as one that runs
669	    quietly, and a dispatch that was never filed must not read as an execution.
670	14. **These rows are a census, and the file says so** — every scheduler run
671	    records every due task, unlike the skill and check counts, which see only
672	    captured sessions. The two populations sit side by side in one file, so the
673	    difference is stated in the file rather than assumed by the reader.
674
