     1	# Prose-to-checks — sweep this repo's pack prose
     2	
     3	Mine the **existing** prose of this repo's packs — each pack's `RULES.md` / `SKILL.md` — for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Where [growth-extract](../growth-extract/task.md) descends the ladder for each *new* lesson and then runs this same skill over its **own** additions before landing them, this task works the *backlog*: standing prose that was always mechanizable but never converted — and that has already survived at least one of those upgrade passes.
     4	
     5	**Weekly, deliberately.** Fresh prose is handled the night it is written, so what reaches this sweep is a slow-moving corpus; a daily re-read of it spent an opus dispatch and an owner-gated PR on a backlog that had not changed.
     6	
     7	You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue whose **Context section is binding scope**: it names the **pack paths** to sweep. Work only those paths — a consuming repo's own local packs by default; Claudinite also its core `packs/`. **Never** edit a read-only mounted canon pack under `.claudinite/shared/`.
     8	
     9	The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`open-pr`**: convert prose to checks in a single owner-approved PR (a check can break CI or misfire, so it is reviewed, not auto-merged).
    10	
    11	## The method lives in the skill
    12	
    13	The conversion method — how to spot an always-testable rule in prose, judge convertibility, author the check plus its **see-it-fail** fixture, and decide what stays prose — is owned by the [**prose-to-checks** skill](../../skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md). Follow it; don't re-derive it here. This worker only frames the unattended run around it.
    14	
    15	## What a run does
    16	
    17	1. **Pick convertible prose** under the Context's pack paths — rules that govern **how we work** (not what the product does — see the skill's first gate), that are *always testable* (a deterministic condition a check could assert), and that no existing check already covers. Prefer the strongest, clearest candidates; converting one or two solid rules well beats churning many shakily.
    18	2. **Convert per the skill** — author the rule module in its owning pack, register it in that pack's `pack.mjs`, and add a **fixture test that fires on a violating input and stays quiet on a clean one** (see-it-fail is mandatory — a check that can't be made confident is left as prose, never shipped broken). Then apply the skill's **deletion test** to the prose the check now stands beside — a paragraph the check fully covers is deleted whole, never trimmed.
    19	3. **Open a PR** — one PR for the run's conversions on a per-run-unique branch, its commit referencing the tracking issue so the `task-lifecycle` gate passes. Keep the repo's offline test suite green before opening.
    20	4. **Log to the tracker** — the standing log is the issue titled exactly **`Claudinite tracker: Prose to Checks`** in this repo. Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number**; create it already closed if missing. **Never open, close, or reopen it**. Log each run as a **dated comment**: the prose converted and the check id it became, or "nothing convertible this run".
    21	
    22	## What this task must never do
    23	
    24	- **Never ship a check that can't be made confident** — the see-it-fail fixture is the gate; an unprovable rule stays prose.
    25	- **Never convert a rule an existing check already covers** — dedupe against the check set first.
    26	- **Never convert a statement of what the product does** — a rule asserting which entities exist, what a surface renders, or that a feature's parts are wired together is a **requirement**, and belongs in the project's executable spec and the suite that proves it. Such a rule is testable, so it passes the check-the-world test on its own; the skill's first gate is what stops it. Found in pack prose it is already mis-homed — leave it and log it, never cement it as a check.
    27	- **Never touch a pack path outside the Context**, and **never edit a mounted canon pack** under `.claudinite/shared/` — a consumer improves only its own local packs.
    28	- **Run on `opus`** — judging convertibility and authoring checks + fixtures is heavy judgment; this task declares `agent_model: opus`.

1	# Scheduled tasks — the per-project scheduling mechanism
2	
3	How a repo's recurring Claudinite work runs (per-project-scheduling
4	[DESIGN](../../docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md), issue #394). A repo
5	schedules **itself**: a vendored hourly **scheduler Action**
6	(`.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml`) evaluates each task's precondition
7	in code and dispatches agent work as `ready-for-agent` `[claudinite-task]`
8	issues, which a per-repo **executor routine** (fired by that label event) runs.
9	The engine is vendored under `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/`; the basics
10	pack owns the conformance guards for the surfaces a repo authors around it —
11	scheduling is baseline Claudinite discipline, present wherever basics is
12	declared (everywhere), not an opt-in feature.
13	
14	The checks below are the doctrine's enforcement; the phased rollout (and the
15	retirement of the legacy central planner it replaces) lives in
16	[MIGRATION.md](../../docs/per-project-scheduling/MIGRATION.md).
17	
18	## What the checks guard
19	
20	- **The scheduler workflow is a thin shim.** The vendored
21	  `claudinite-scheduler.yml` carries a single **hourly** cron on a repo-hashed
22	  minute constrained to **:10–:50** (the one repo-specific value in the stub —
23	  `engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs`, a pure function of the repo full name that
24	  bootstrap stamps in and baselining re-derives), a `concurrency` group, a
25	  `workflow_dispatch` trigger, and a call into the vendored engine entry — no logic of its own
26	  (schema and behaviour changes ride the vendor refresh, not workflow edits). It
27	  is the repo's **only** cron. Recurring work that had its own cron'd workflow
28	  becomes a **task**, and that workflow is deleted — its steps move into the
29	  task's worker. Don't keep it as a dispatch-only workflow for the task to fire:
30	  that is two files and two edit sites for one job, and a workflow whose only
31	  caller is the thing that replaced it. (A workflow that must run *as an Action*
32	  for something a task cannot reach — an Actions-only secret, say — is the
33	  exception, and even then the task owns the schedule.) Off-band or multiple
34	  crons, or a missing concurrency/dispatch guard, break staggering, double-run
35	  safety, or manual runs.
36	
37	- **Every task declaration carries the full contract.** A `tasks/<name>/task.mjs`
38	  default-exports `id` (matching its directory), `frequency` (`hourly | daily-2h
39	  | daily-1h | daily | daily+1h | weekly | monthly`), `precondition_signals` (the collector
40	  vocabulary), `agent_model` (`opus | sonnet | haiku | none`), `expected_outcome` (`none |
41	  open-pr | merged-pr`), and a `precondition`. An agentic task (`agent_model !==
42	  none`) also carries `agent_instructions`, the worker file the agent reads; a
43	  `none` task runs no agent, so the field is not applicable and is omitted. The
44	  scheduler and executor read agent_model/expected_outcome/frequency from this file — never from the dispatch
45	  issue — so an illegal or missing value means a task never fires, fires wrong,
46	  or writes past its declared ceiling. The same contract
47	  (`engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs`) is re-validated at run time, so the
48	  static and runtime views can't drift. Optionally, `session_scope` (`self` default
49	  | `fleet`) declares whether the task reaches only its own repo or across the
50	  owner's repos: a `fleet` task dispatches to the `ready-for-agent-fleet` label so a
51	  distinct, broader-scoped executor runs it, keeping the fleet-wide session grant
52	  off every ordinary project's `ready-for-agent` (self) executor. **Declaring
53	  `fleet` routes the dispatch; it does not create the routine that runs it** — that
54	  second, label-wired routine exists only in the canon repo, and its launcher prompt
55	  must end in the word `fleet` (the executor defaults an unnamed scope to `self` and
56	  then declines the dispatch as another scope's). Get either wrong and the task fails
57	  *silently and forever*: the session stops without commenting, the scheduler re-arms
58	  the issue hourly, and nothing ever runs it.
59	
60	- **Every run is bounded.** An agentic task (`agent_model !== none`) declares
61	  `agent_execution_timeout` — seconds bounding the agentic run
62	  (agent-preprocessing [DESIGN](../../docs/agent-preprocessing/DESIGN.md) §2, §6).
63	  There is no platform wall-clock kill for a launched executor session, so the
64	  bound is best-effort: the executor surfaces it into the subagent's brief ("fail
65	  after N minutes") and the stale-`agent-running` backstop catches a dead session.
66	  Set it generously — extreme protection against a runaway, not a scheduling knob.
67	
68	- **A task says which repo secrets it needs.** Preprocessing runs Action-side, so
69	  repo Actions secrets are reachable there and nowhere else in a task's life (an
70	  executor session carries none). A task lists what it needs in `required_secrets`;
71	  the wiring converge stamps each name into the scheduler workflow, so a worker
72	  reads it as ordinary environment, and baselining asks the owner (one standing
73	  issue) for any the repo hasn't configured. The adoption interview's posture, not
74	  a gate — nothing fails; the task that needs the secret just doesn't work yet. The
75	  consequence worth designing around: **a workflow that exists only to hold a
76	  secret is redundant** — fold its work into the task's preprocessing rather than
77	  dispatching and polling a second workflow from an agent.
78	
79	Both guards are **relevance-first**: inert until their artifact exists, so
80	on a repo with neither artifact they are a no-op.
81	
82	## The task folder
83	
84	One directory per task — `<pack>/tasks/<name>/` — holding **`task.mjs`** (the
85	self-contained declaration + `precondition(signals, config)`, the eligibility
86	gate as pure code) beside **`task.md`** (the worker spec the executing agent
87	follows), plus any deterministic helpers. The precondition both asserts
88	need-to-run and pre-decides scope: its `context` lines land verbatim in the
89	dispatch issue as binding constraints the agent may not re-litigate. `agent_model:
90	none` replaces the worker doc with an inline `.mjs` the scheduler runs directly —
91	no agent, no issue. This is the scheduled-task shape of the unattended-agents
92	routine-folder convention; the issue-driven-dispatch security rule (the issue is
93	data, the task path is code-validated, agent_model/expected_outcome come from the repo) lives
94	with that skill's agent practices.
95	
96	## A precondition may claim the whole run
97	
98	A verdict can carry **`exclusive: true`** beside `run: true` — *if I run this
99	cycle, I run alone*. Every other due task whose precondition said run is
100	**deferred**: no preprocessing, no dispatch issue, no inline work. It is there
101	because the hourly cron is not hourly (see the `github-actions-scheduling`
102	skill): a run that fires hours late finds several daily slots due at once, so the
103	hour of staging between the daily anchors collapses and a task anchored to run
104	*before* the others runs *beside* them. Baselining is the case it was built for —
105	it converges the mount, the wiring and the migration notes everything else then
106	executes against.
107	
108	Claim sparingly, and **bound the claim at both ends**. A deferred slot is spent,
109	not queued: the run succeeds, the watermark moves past it, and that task runs
110	again at its *next* slot — tomorrow, or next week. So a claim on the routine case
111	quietly halves the fleet's throughput, and a claim with no upper bound (a
112	condition that stays true while something is broken) stops the repo doing
113	anything at all for as long as the breakage lasts. Baselining's shape is the
114	model: claim when the mount is more than a day stale, stop claiming past three
115	days, when it is a human's problem rather than a missed fire.
116	
117	## The dispatch labels are a scheduler vocabulary
118	
119	**Both ready labels are triggers**, so they belong on dispatch issues alone — never put
120	`ready-for-agent` or `ready-for-agent-fleet` on an ordinary issue, from a task or by hand.
121	Applying one starts an executor session that will find no valid dispatch and stop.
122	`agent-running` and `needs-human` carry no trigger and are the right vocabulary for a task
123	that needs to mark an issue as claimed or handed to a human; a task reusing them owns their
124	whole lifecycle on its own issues, since the scheduler's stale-claim backstop only converges
125	`[claudinite-task]` dispatch issues.
126	
127	Which ready label a task dispatches under follows from its `session_scope`, and the executor
128	session started by that label is the one with the matching reach — a `fleet` task's session
129	has the owner's repos in its sources, a `self` task's has this repo alone. The task declares
130	the scope; nothing downstream re-decides it.
131	
132	## A dormant project runs nothing
133	
134	A project nobody is working on declares itself dormant in `.claudinite-checks.json`:
135	
136	```json
137	"dormant": true
138	```
139	
140	The scheduler stops before evaluating anything; the [fleet sweeps](../sheepdog/README.md)
141	skip it; sessions are unaffected. Delete it to wake.

  issue) for any the repo hasn't configured. The adoption interview's posture, not
  a gate — nothing fails; the task that needs the secret just doesn't work yet. The
  consequence worth designing around: **a workflow that exists only to hold a
  secret is redundant** — fold its work into the task's preprocessing rather than
  dispatching and polling a second workflow from an agent.

Both guards are **relevance-first**: inert until their artifact exists, so
on a repo with neither artifact they are a no-op.

## The task folder

One directory per task — `<pack>/tasks/<name>/` — holding **`task.mjs`** (the
self-contained declaration + `precondition(signals, config)`, the eligibility
gate as pure code) beside **`task.md`** (the worker spec the executing agent
follows), plus any deterministic helpers. The precondition both asserts
need-to-run and pre-decides scope: its `context` lines land verbatim in the
dispatch issue as binding constraints the agent may not re-litigate. `agent_model:
none` replaces the worker doc with an inline `.mjs` the scheduler runs directly —
no agent, no issue. This is the scheduled-task shape of the unattended-agents
routine-folder convention; the issue-driven-dispatch security rule (the issue is
data, the task path is code-validated, agent_model/expected_outcome come from the repo) lives
with that skill's agent practices.

## A precondition may claim the whole run

A verdict can carry **`exclusive: true`** beside `run: true` — *if I run this
cycle, I run alone*. Every other due task whose precondition said run is
**deferred**: no preprocessing, no dispatch issue, no inline work. It is there
because the hourly cron is not hourly (see the `github-actions-scheduling`
skill): a run that fires hours late finds several daily slots due at once, so the
hour of staging between the daily anchors collapses and a task anchored to run
*before* the others runs *beside* them. Baselining is the case it was built for —
it converges the mount, the wiring and the migration notes everything else then
executes against.

Claim sparingly, and **bound the claim at both ends**. A deferred slot is spent,
not queued: the run succeeds, the watermark moves past it, and that task runs
again at its *next* slot — tomorrow, or next week. So a claim on the routine case
quietly halves the fleet's throughput, and a claim with no upper bound (a
condition that stays true while something is broken) stops the repo doing
anything at all for as long as the breakage lasts. Baselining's shape is the
model: claim when the mount is more than a day stale, stop claiming past three
days, when it is a human's problem rather than a missed fire.

## The dispatch labels are a scheduler vocabulary

**Both ready labels are triggers**, so they belong on dispatch issues alone — never put
`ready-for-agent` or `ready-for-agent-fleet` on an ordinary issue, from a task or by hand.
Applying one starts an executor session that will find no valid dispatch and stop.
`agent-running` and `needs-human` carry no trigger and are the right vocabulary for a task
that needs to mark an issue as claimed or handed to a human; a task reusing them owns their
whole lifecycle on its own issues, since the scheduler's stale-claim backstop only converges
`[claudinite-task]` dispatch issues.

Which ready label a task dispatches under follows from its `session_scope`, and the executor
session started by that label is the one with the matching reach — a `fleet` task's session
has the owner's repos in its sources, a `self` task's has this repo alone. The task declares
the scope; nothing downstream re-decides it.

## A dormant project runs nothing

A project nobody is working on declares itself dormant in `.claudinite-checks.json`:

```json
"dormant": true
```

The scheduler stops before evaluating anything; the [fleet sweeps](../sheepdog/README.md)
skip it; sessions are unaffected. Delete it to wake.

     1	# Fleet freshness — is each covered member still keeping up?
     2	
     3	**This task runs no agent.** It is `agent_model: none` with `agent_preprocessing: node worker.mjs`, so the whole pass is the deterministic [`worker.mjs`](worker.mjs) the scheduler runs as a subprocess, which calls its sibling in this folder, the sweep ([`check-fleet-freshness.mjs`](check-fleet-freshness.mjs)). This file is the human-facing record of what that worker does; there is no dispatch issue and no subagent.
     4	
     5	## Why it exists
     6	
     7	Per-project scheduling made every member maintain **itself**: its own vendored `claudinite-scheduler.yml` fires hourly, and its `baselining` task re-vendors the mount from canon. That is the right architecture — and it removed the last thing that ever looked at a member from the **outside**.
     8	
     9	A member whose scheduler was never vendored, whose workflow was deleted or auto-disabled, or whose baselining has been failing for a fortnight is now invisible. It is still `covered` to the census (it carries a declaration). It files no failure issue, because nothing runs there to fail. **Self-maintenance cannot detect its own absence.** This sweep is the outside look.
    10	
    11	## What it does
    12	
    13	Weekly, over the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT: read this (sheepdog) repo's `sheepdog` pack entry `config` (`owner`, `exclude`, `canonRepo`, `staleDays`), enumerate every repo that owner owns, and for each **covered** member make three reads — its `.claudinite-checks.json` (for `claudinite.ref`), whether it carries `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml`, and canon's comparison of that ref against canon's default branch. Then classify by **root cause**, in this precedence:
    14	
    15	| state | meaning |
    16	|---|---|
    17	| `no-stamp` | declares packs but was never vendored — no engine on disk at all |
    18	| `no-scheduler` | no vendored scheduler workflow, so no cron, so it will never baseline itself; every other symptom is downstream of this |
    19	| `ref-not-on-trunk` | the stamped ref is not a canon commit, or not an ancestor of canon's default branch — vendoring's #328 anti-rewind guard refuses to write, so the repo is **wedged**, not merely late |
    20	| `behind` | on trunk, but stamped at a commit older than `staleDays` while canon has moved on — baselining has stopped landing |
    21	| `fresh` | at canon head, or behind it only within the window |
    22	
    23	It publishes the picture to the run summary and converges **one drift issue per unhealthy member** in this repo, labelled `fleet-drift`: opened while unhealthy, closed `completed` once fresh again, closed `not planned` once the repo leaves the fleet (excluded, deleted, archived, or no longer covered), reopened if it regresses.
    24	
    25	It **reports; it does not repair** — `expected_outcome: none`, and the issue body carries the fix for the specific state it found.
    26	
    27	## A dormant member is not measured
    28	
    29	A member that declares `"dormant": true` ([the scheduler's gate](../../../basics/scheduled-tasks.md)) is skipped before its stamp is read, and any open drift issue for it is closed *not planned*. Its scheduler is stopped, so its mount falls behind **by design** — reporting that would nag a repo for obeying its own declaration. It is counted in its own column of the summary, never as a failure.
    30	
    31	The test is `isDormant`, re-exported from the engine rather than re-implemented here: a sweep with a private notion of dormancy would nag exactly the repos that had already opted out.
    32	
    33	## Freshness, not coverage
    34	
    35	The [census](../fleet-census/task.md) asks the prior question — is a repo covered **at all** — and opens adoption issues. This sweep takes coverage as given and asks whether that coverage still **means** anything. An uncovered repo is skipped here, never double-reported.
    36	
    37	## The one assumption
    38	
    39	Baselining reverts a stamp-only bump, so `claudinite.updated` advances only when canon actually changed that member's vendor set. Age of the **stamped ref** is therefore the honest liveness measure, and `behind` reads *"this member has not picked canon up in `staleDays`"* — not *"canon moved"*.
    40	
    41	It can still misfire on a member whose vendor set genuinely saw no change in the window. `staleDays` (default **14**) is the knob, and the drift issue says so rather than leaving the reader to guess.
    42	
    43	## Not a fleet mechanism
    44	
    45	Its *implementation* reads every repo under the owner, but its declaration, scheduling and lifecycle are those of **any pack task**: it is active because this repo declares the `sheepdog` pack, and it runs on this repo's ordinary scheduler. It declares no `fleet` signal and no `fleet` session scope — the cross-repo reach lives in the implementation, never in the wiring.
    46	
    47	## Failure is loud
    48	
    49	A member whose probe **errors** is classified `unknown`, never behind: no drift issue is opened for it, no open issue is closed on its behalf, and the sweep exits non-zero. The scheduler treats a non-zero preprocessing subprocess as a failed task and converges a `needs-human` issue, so an unusable token or scope escalates rather than silently shrinking the fleet.

    11	// over FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN (the account-spanning PAT — the Action token sees only
    12	// this repo), while the delivery WRITES this repo's own PR over the ordinary Action
    13	// GITHUB_TOKEN.
    14	//
    15	// Failure is the escalation path. The sweep THROWS when its config or token is
    16	// unusable, or when enumeration comes back empty; this worker turns that into a
    17	// non-zero exit, and the scheduler treats a non-zero preprocessing subprocess as a
    18	// failed task — it converges one open `needs-human` issue for the task family
    19	// (engine/scheduler/run.mjs) instead of handing off to any agent.
    20	
    21	import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';

    23	import { main as sweep, FLEET_USAGE_PATH } from './aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs';

    29	// `generatedAt` changes every day, so comparing the whole file would open a PR daily
    30	// even on a fleet where nothing moved. Compare everything else: an unchanged fleet
    31	// re-stamps nothing and opens nothing.
    32	export function unchanged(priorText, nextText) {
    33	  if (priorText === null) return false;
    34	  const strip = (text) => {
    35	    try { const { generatedAt, ...rest } = JSON.parse(text); return JSON.stringify(rest); } catch { return null; }

    41	export async function main() {

    43	  // fleet config, and the one the aggregate lands in — from GITHUB_REPOSITORY.

########## packs/sheepdog/tasks/fleet-usage/task.md
     1	# Fleet usage — recompute the fleet-wide skill-usage aggregate
     2	
     3	**This task runs no agent.** It is `agent_model: none` with `agent_preprocessing: node worker.mjs`, so the whole pass is the deterministic [`worker.mjs`](worker.mjs) the scheduler runs as a subprocess, which calls its sibling in this folder, the sweep ([`aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs`](aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs)). This file is the human-facing record of what that worker does; there is no dispatch issue and no subagent.
     4	
     5	## What it does
     6	
     7	Daily, over the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT: read this (sheepdog) repo's `sheepdog` pack entry `config`, enumerate every repo that owner owns, read each covered member's `.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json` at its default branch, and rebuild `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` in this repo on an auto-merging PR.
     8	
     9	A **stateless full recompute** — the file is a pure function of the members' current files. Idempotent by definition, self-healing after any past error, and cheap to no-op: a fleet whose numbers did not move produces the same file and opens no PR.
    10	
    11	## What it answers that a member cannot
    12	
    13	Each member folds its own numbers, so each can say whether a skill ever loads *there*. Whether a skill earns its place at all is a fleet-shaped question: never loading in one repo may only mean it isn't that repo's subject, while never loading in **any** of them means the trigger is mis-described — or that the content should never have been gated behind a skill in the first place. Only a view across every member separates those.
    14	
    15	The **conformance checks** are carried at the same grain and for exactly the same reason, and they answer a sharper question, because a check failure is an observed correction rather than an inferred one: the finding went back into the session and the agent fixed it before the work left the branch. A rule with steady failures across the fleet is a guard earning its keep; a rule that has never fired in *any* member is unreachable or describing something that does not happen; a rule firing on nearly every run is a default the corpus should change rather than a violation worth blocking on. The `errors` counter reads differently from all three — enforcement was silently off — and is the one number here whose right value is zero.
    16	
    17	The grain is therefore full — week × repo × skill, and week × repo × rule, for history, plus each member's current day window verbatim — with nothing pre-summed. Every coarser view stays derivable from the file; a summary that threw the grain away would not.
    18	
    19	A member still on an older fold carries no `checks` key. It lands as an empty check row, never as an exception: the sweep leads the members' upgrades, so that is the normal state for a while.
    20	
    21	## Coverage gaps are reported, not skipped
    22	
    23	A covered member with no usage file (not folding yet), or one whose file cannot be read, is listed in `coverage.absent` with the reason — census-style. A denominator with an invisible hole in it is worse than no denominator at all.
    24	
    25	## A dormant member leaves the denominator
    26	
    27	A member that declares `"dormant": true` ([the scheduler's gate](../../../basics/scheduled-tasks.md)) is dropped from every rate and listed under `coverage.dormant` — distinct from `coverage.absent`, because "not in the race" and "should be folding and isn't" are different facts. Averaging a deliberately silent repo in would drag every fleet-wide number toward zero as the fleet accumulates finished projects. The test is `isDormant`, re-exported from the engine, so the sweep and the member's own scheduler cannot disagree.
    28	
    29	## It is a sample, not a census
    30	
    31	The file carries a `_note` saying so. Its whole population is *captured* sessions: sessions that merged, plus sessions that ended cleanly enough for the SessionEnd capture to fire. A session whose container was reclaimed, or that crashed, is invisible to every number in it.
    32	
    33	The check counts sit inside a narrower boundary still, and the note says that too: they are what a *session* saw. A CI run counts when the session pulled its job log in — which is what "the agent was in the loop on it" means, and it is the loop that produces the correction — while a nightly or post-merge run nobody looked at does not, because nothing was corrected. CI can only see a run that *printed* something, so its share rides separately as `ciRuns`/`ciFailures` rather than skewing a rate. The under-count is one-directional — every check number is a floor on activations, never an over-count — which is what keeps "the checks caught N things fleet-wide this week" a claim worth making.
    34	
    35	## Not a fleet mechanism
    36	
    37	Its *implementation* reads every repo under the owner, but its declaration, scheduling and lifecycle are those of **any pack task**: it is active because this repo declares the `sheepdog` pack, and it runs on this repo's ordinary scheduler. It declares no `fleet` signal and no `fleet` session scope — the cross-repo reach lives in the implementation, never in the wiring.

     1	// chrome-extension-release task: store-release — the pack-contributed release
     2	// trigger (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §6). STRUCTURAL Stage 2: `model: 'none'`
     3	// means the whole decision is code and there is NO agent and NO dispatch issue —
     4	// the scheduler runs the inline `worker.mjs` directly. This task ABSORBS the
     5	// release workflow's own independent 00:30 cron: the workflow becomes push +
     6	// workflow_dispatch only, and this task is the one place that fires its daily
     7	// leg, so the scheduler stays the repo's only cron (DESIGN §3, decision §11.6).
     8	//
     9	// Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export.
    10	
    11	const norm = (v) => String(v ?? '').replace(/^v/, '').trim(); // compare tags/versions modulo a leading 'v'
    12	
    13	export default {
    14	  id: 'store-release',
    15	  frequency: 'daily',              // the 04:00 slot (DESIGN §2) — replaces the workflow's own 00:30 cron
    16	  precondition_signals: ['release', 'commits'],
    17	  agent_model: 'none',                   // pure code — no agent (agent-preprocessing DESIGN §4)
    18	  expected_outcome: 'none',                 // it only TRIGGERS the gated publish workflow; publishing stays behind that workflow's own guards
    19	  agent_preprocessing: 'node worker.mjs',      // the scheduler runs this as a subprocess (cwd = this task dir) — DESIGN §3
    20	  agent_preprocessing_timeout: 120,            // the dispatch is a quick REST call; a tight bound (the await-the-run Stage 2 would widen it)
    21	
    22	  // Detect a deployable change since the last release, entirely in code:
    23	  //   (a) the manifest version has advanced past the latest published release
    24	  //       (an unreleased bump — the same signal the old run_daily gate used), OR
    25	  //   (b) a substantive default-branch commit landed in the window (a real ship).
    26	  // Ship-path precision (the daily job's `ship_paths` filter) is NOT re-derived
    27	  // here — .github/release.config isn't in a precondition's scope — because the
    28	  // dispatched daily workflow does the authoritative shipped-file diff vs the
    29	  // latest release tag and no-ops when nothing shippable moved. So the
    30	  // precondition is the cheap pre-filter; the workflow is the exact gate.
    31	  precondition(signals) {
    32	    const rel = signals.release ?? {};
    33	    const shipped = norm(rel.manifestVersion);
    34	    const released = norm(rel.latestTag);
    35	    const manifestAhead = shipped !== '' && shipped !== released;
    36	    const substantive = signals.commits?.substantiveChange === true;
    37	
    38	    if (manifestAhead) {
    39	      return { run: true, reason: released ? `manifest ${shipped} is ahead of released ${released}` : `manifest ${shipped}, no release yet` };
    40	    }
    41	    if (substantive) {
    42	      return { run: true, reason: 'substantive default-branch change in the window — let the daily release workflow diff shipped files' };
    43	    }
    44	    return { run: false, reason: 'manifest matches the latest release and no substantive change in the window' };
    45	  },
    46	};
########## packs/chrome-extension-release/tasks/store-release/worker.mjs
     1	// store-release worker (agent-preprocessing DESIGN §3/§4). This task is
     2	// `agent_model: 'none'` with `agent_preprocessing: 'node worker.mjs'`, so the
     3	// scheduler runs THIS FILE as a subprocess (cwd = this task dir) bounded by
     4	// `agent_preprocessing_timeout` — there is no agent and no dispatch issue on
     5	// success. Its one job is to TRIGGER the repo's vendored `Release to Chrome
     6	// Store` orchestrator in daily mode and hand off: the orchestrator's `daily` leg
     7	// does the authoritative shipped-file diff, patch bump, and gated submission, so
     8	// this worker never decides what ships and never publishes anything itself.
     9	//
    10	// This absorbs the release workflow's retired 00:30 cron (per-project-scheduling
    11	// decision §11.6): the scheduler is the repo's only cron, and this is the surface
    12	// that fires the daily release.
    13	//
    14	// Self-contained — imports only node builtins (the pack-independence barrier
    15	// forbids reaching into the engine). It reads its context from the CLAUDINITE_* /
    16	// GITHUB_* env the scheduler injects and calls the Actions REST API directly over
    17	// the injected GITHUB_TOKEN, the one sanctioned non-MCP surface (DESIGN §10). A
    18	// non-204 dispatch, or a throw, exits non-zero — the scheduler then converges the
    19	// task to needs-human.
    20	
    21	import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
    22	
    23	// The vendored orchestrator's file name and the dispatch mode that runs its daily
    24	// leg (release-workflows.mjs STUB_FILE / RELEASE.md §Workflow). Bare literals —
    25	// this worker imports nothing from the engine, and the name is the
    26	// conformance-pinned fingerprint.
    27	const ORCHESTRATOR_FILE = 'chrome-extension-release.yml';
    28	const DISPATCH_MODE = 'daily';
    29	const API = 'https://api.github.com';
    30	
    31	// A minimal Actions-REST call over the injected GITHUB_TOKEN. Returns { status }.
    32	async function gh(path, { method = 'GET', body } = {}) {
    33	  const res = await fetch(`${API}${path}`, {
    34	    method,
    35	    headers: {
    36	      authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN}`,
    37	      accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
    38	      'x-github-api-version': '2022-11-28',
    39	      ...(body ? { 'content-type': 'application/json' } : {}),
    40	    },
    41	    body: body ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,
    42	  });
    43	  return { status: res.status };
    44	}
    45	
    46	export async function main() {
    47	  const repo = process.env.CLAUDINITE_REPO || process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY;
    48	  const ref = process.env.CLAUDINITE_DEFAULT_BRANCH || 'main';
    49	  const slotId = process.env.CLAUDINITE_SLOT_ID || '';
    50	  if (!repo) { console.error('store-release: no repo in env (CLAUDINITE_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY)'); process.exit(1); }
    51	  if (!process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN) { console.error('store-release: no GITHUB_TOKEN in env'); process.exit(1); }
    52	
    53	  // Fire the orchestrator's daily leg via workflow_dispatch — the orchestrator is
    54	  // push + workflow_dispatch only now (its own cron retired), so this is the sole
    55	  // scheduled trigger of the daily release. A 204 is success.
    56	  const res = await gh(`/repos/${repo}/actions/workflows/${ORCHESTRATOR_FILE}/dispatches`, {
    57	    method: 'POST',
    58	    body: { ref, inputs: { mode: DISPATCH_MODE } },
    59	  });
    60	  if (res.status !== 204) {
    61	    console.error(`store-release [${slotId}]: dispatching ${ORCHESTRATOR_FILE} (mode ${DISPATCH_MODE}) on ${ref} returned ${res.status}`);
    62	    process.exit(1);
    63	  }
    64	  console.log(`store-release [${slotId}]: dispatched ${ORCHESTRATOR_FILE} (mode ${DISPATCH_MODE}) on ${ref}`);
    65	
    66	  // STUB (unchanged from the pre-conversion worker): this triggers the daily
    67	  // release and hands off. The full Stage-2 would then AWAIT the dispatched run
    68	  // (poll it to conclusion) and report at completion — now safe to add, because
    69	  // the subprocess is bounded by agent_preprocessing_timeout, but it needs a
    70	  // generous timeout and is left as the next increment.
    71	}
    72	
    73	// Run only when invoked directly (the scheduler's `node worker.mjs`), never on
    74	// import — so a test can import { main } without firing a real dispatch.
    75	if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {
    76	  main();
    77	}
########## packs/product-wiki/tasks/wiki-growth/task.mjs
     1	// product-wiki task: wiki-growth — one research-and-refine pass over the repo's
     2	// product wikis (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §6). Worker: task.md.
     3	//
     4	// WEEKLY, not daily and not commit-gated: research arrives on the world's clock,
     5	// not the repo's, and a nightly high-model pass economically pressures
     6	// fabrication (the Karpathy LLM-wiki cadence). The `commits` signal is declared
     7	// only so the precondition can note recent product-relevant movement in context;
     8	// the run itself is scheduled by frequency, not triggered by a commit.

    10	// The open-growth-PR preflight stays in task.md, and is NOT subsumed by the
    11	// scheduler: planDispatch guards at most one open dispatch ISSUE per (pack,
    12	// task) — it never looks at pull requests. A completed run converges and closes
    13	// its own dispatch issue while leaving the growth PR open for review, so the
    14	// next weekly slot finds no open issue in the family and dispatches freely. The
    15	// preflight is the only thing standing between an unreviewed PR and a second
    16	// round of research stacked on top of it; do not delete it on the strength of
    17	// the issue guard.
    18	//
    19	// The precondition itself deliberately never declines: a wiki grows on research
    20	// availability, not repo activity, so there is no cheaper gate to apply than the
    21	// weekly slot, and the worker's own stop condition (no citable material → no
    22	// branch, no PR) is the real "nothing to do" outcome.
    23	//
    24	// Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export.

    27	  id: 'wiki-growth',
    28	  frequency: 'weekly',             // fires at the weekly anchor (DESIGN §2) — the world's clock, not the repo's
    29	  precondition_signals: ['commits'],
    30	  agent_model: 'opus',                   // open-web research + curation is the heaviest judgment, and the PR review gate is the last catch for fabrication
    31	  expected_outcome: 'open-pr',              // web-researched claims entering a knowledge base need the human review gate — never merged, never pushed to default
    32	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
    33	  agent_execution_timeout: 2700,            // open-web research is the least predictable of the tasks — very generous
    34	
    35	  // The weekly slot IS the trigger — there is no cheaper gate to apply, because a
    36	  // wiki grows on research availability, not repo activity. Always run when due;
    37	  // the worker's own stop condition (no citable material → no branch, no PR) is
    38	  // the real "nothing to do" outcome, and task.md's open-growth-PR preflight —
    39	  // not the scheduler, which guards issues only — prevents stacking a second

     1	# wiki-growth worker
     2	
     3	One compile-once/refine-in-place research pass over the repo's product wikis (the Karpathy LLM-wiki pattern):
     4	read what the wiki already knows, research only what its own backlog flags, write it back cited. **Most runs
     5	find little or nothing — no new citable material means no branch, no PR, and that is the documented good
     6	outcome.** A padded or fabricated update is worse than none.
     7	
     8	You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue; GitHub access is the session's
     9	**GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`) — never `gh`/`curl`/a clone. "Default branch" below means the repo's
    10	actual default branch. The wiki set is derived **structurally**: every `README.md` at depth ≥ 2 under
    11	`product-wiki/`, excluding the `product-wiki/product-requirements/` and `product-wiki/sample-data/` subtrees.
    12	
    13	The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`open-pr`**: it may open a PR but never merges one and never pushes to
    14	the default branch.
    15	
    16	## Preflight
    17	
    18	**Before researching**, list this repo's open PRs carrying the **`product-wiki-growth` label** — the marker
    19	every PR of this family applies to itself, and the only thing that identifies one. If one is open, do **not**
    20	stack a second round of unreviewed research on it — add one dated nudge comment on that PR and stop.
    21	
    22	This is the *only* guard against that stacking — nothing upstream covers it. The scheduler's at-most-one-open
    23	guard is about **dispatch issues**, not pull requests: a completed run converges and closes its own dispatch
    24	issue while leaving this task's PR open for the owner to review, so the next weekly slot sees an empty issue
    25	family and dispatches normally. Expect to find an open growth PR whenever the last one hasn't been reviewed
    26	yet; that is the ordinary case this preflight exists for, not an anomaly.
    27	
    28	## Method
    29	
    30	1. **Read every wiki page end to end** (`get_file_contents`), the `## Open questions` and `## Growth log`
    31	   sections first-class. Never re-derive a claim that is already cited and current.
    32	2. **Pick the one or two open questions** across the set most worth this run; also spot-check one or two
    33	   existing citations for staleness (a dead link, a superseded stat). If the Context flagged a product-wiki
    34	   change in the window, spot-check the pages it may have superseded.
    35	3. **Research.** *Web mode* (WebSearch/WebFetch available): the open web. *Repo-derived mode* (web tools
    36	   absent — do not fail, do not fake): citable repo-native signal only — new feature-request/extractor-request
    37	   issues, merged PRs, issue/PR discussion carrying user-side signal — each citable to its own GitHub URL.
    38	4. **Write into the relevant wiki page(s) only**, per the pack's RULES.md: cite every claim in that page's
    39	   `## Sources`; correct a wrong or superseded claim with a note of why, never a silent deletion; touch
    40	   `product-wiki/sample-data/` only when a new claim needs an illustrative example; **never write
    41	   `product-wiki/product-requirements/`** — a finding that should move a requirement gets a growth-log note
    42	   (and a repo issue) and waits for a human.
    43	5. **Reconcile the page's `## Key insights` header** with what the body now says. It leads the page, it is
    44	   bullets only, and it is capped (seven bullets, 140 characters each — about one line) — so a new insight
    45	   that belongs at the top usually displaces a weaker one rather than being appended. Each bullet is one
    46	   finding in plain words: no qualifying clause, no citation, no hedge, and preferably something a reader
    47	   who knows the field would *not* already assume. Judging obviousness is hard, so when in doubt keep the
    48	   line rather than agonising — short and slightly obvious beats long and careful. Rewrite a bullet the run
    49	   superseded (the correction and its *why* live in the body, not in the header); leave the header alone
    50	   when the run changed nothing about the page's top-line understanding. **Never restate the header as a
    51	   table of contents** — each bullet is a finding a reader can act on.
    52	6. **One dated `## Growth log` entry per touched page** (`- **YYYY-MM-DD** — what changed`).
    53	7. **Update `## Open questions` both directions** — remove what this run answered, add what its research
    54	   surfaced.
    55	
    56	## Stop condition
    57	
    58	Neither mode yields citable material → stop. No commit, no log entry, no PR.
    59	
    60	## Delivery
    61	
    62	A unique branch per run, commits touching only `product-wiki/**` minus `product-requirements/`, one
    63	**PR — never merged, never pushed to the default branch directly** — carrying the **`product-wiki-growth`
    64	label**. The label is load-bearing: it is how the next run's preflight sees this PR at all, so a PR opened
    65	without it will be stacked on by the following slot.
    66	Web-researched claims entering a committed knowledge base need the review gate. PR body: the question(s)
    67	researched, what changed where, the citations added, and the open questions left for the next run.
    68	
    69	## Tracking
    70	
    71	Standing issue found by exact title **"Claudinite tracker: Product Wiki Growth"** in the repo — found by
    72	title, never by number, never opened/closed as state (open it if missing). One dated comment when a pass
    73	**grew** (`grew (PR #N): <one line>`) or was **blocked** (`blocked: <why>` — the human-visible convergence for
    74	a failed unattended run). Clean no-ops stay silent — the pack's freshness advisory is the prolonged-silence
    75	observer.
    76	
    77	`agent_model: opus` — open-web research plus curation is judgment-heavy, and the PR review gate is the last catch for
    78	fabrication.
    79	
    80	## What this worker must never do
    81	
    82	Edit `product-wiki/product-requirements/`; edit anything outside `product-wiki/`; create new wiki folders
    83	(automation refines existing pages — a human creates a wiki deliberately); write an uncited claim; delete a
    84	claim without a superseded note; leave a `## Key insights` header asserting what the body it heads no longer
    85	says; pad a growth log, a header, or a wiki page to look productive; merge or approve its own
    86	PR; schedule anything (no cron, no `schedule:` workflow); touch the shared canon.

########## .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/tasks/growth-promote/task.mjs
     1	// canon-curation task: growth-promote — the growth lifecycle's CENTRAL stage
     2	// (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §6, table 2). Reads the participating members'
     3	// local packs, generalizes the portable lessons, and opens an owner-gated PR
     4	// against the canon. A fleet-scoped task: it runs only on the canon repo's own
     5	// scheduler (only the canon declares canon-curation), and its precondition reads
     6	// the `fleet` signal — the members aggregate over the fleet PAT.
     7	//
     8	// Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export.
     9	//
    10	// "Central, once" is enforced by declaration cardinality, not orchestrator
    11	// wiring: only the canon home repo declares canon-curation, so this task exists
    12	// nowhere else. No barrier — promote reads whatever is already MERGED on members'
    13	// mains, so a lesson extracted tonight (03:00, extract) is promoted this same
    14	// 04:00 run when its auto-merge landed in time, else the next night (DESIGN §2).
    15	
    16	export default {
    17	  id: 'growth-promote',
    18	  frequency: 'daily',                    // the 04:00 slot — after the fleet's 03:00 extracts (DESIGN §2)
    19	  precondition_signals: ['fleet'],       // canon-only aggregate: which members changed their local packs
    20	  session_scope: 'fleet',                // reads every member's local packs → runs in the FLEET executor (ready-for-agent-fleet), not the self one
    21	  agent_model: 'opus',                   // portability, dedup-vs-corpus, and routing are the heaviest judgment

    23	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
    24	  agent_execution_timeout: 2700,         // reading N members + generalizing + authoring a PR — generous bound, extreme protection
    25

    27	  // participant declares grow_with_claudinite and carries local packs (the only
    28	  // source promote reads); the growth entry's `{ config: { promote: false } }`
    29	  // opts a member out of promotion while it keeps extracting/deduping locally
    30	  // (absent or true = participate). A member whose local packs didn't move in the
    31	  // window has nothing new to lift up — so the daily trigger targets exactly the
    32	  // changed set, and the executor's Context binds the worker to those members.

     1	# Growth — promote lessons into the canon (the central stage)
     2	
     3	The [growth lifecycle](../../README.md)'s central stage: read the target members' local packs, lift the portable lessons into the shared canon, and open a PR against the canon's default branch **for the owner to approve**. Declared only by the Claudinite home repo, so it runs **once, centrally**, never per project.
     4	
     5	You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent-fleet` issue whose **Context section is binding scope**: it names the exact target members (those whose local packs changed in the window). Work exactly that list — the fleet enumeration already happened in the precondition; **do not enumerate the fleet yourself or widen past the Context**.
     6	
     7	The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`open-pr`**: promotion is the **judgment gate before shared canon**. It opens a PR and **never arms auto-merge** — the owner approves it. But don't lean on that review as the portability check: [extract](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-extract/task.md) stays project-specific by design, so it's no second opinion, and the owner can't re-derive every portability call. This task's judgment is the real thing between a bad rule and every project that reads the canon — keep the bar high (dedupe against the whole corpus; default to reject when unsure).
     8	
     9	## Conventions used in this doc
    10	
    11	- **GitHub access is MCP-only** (`mcp__github__*`). You are outside each member repo — read its files over the API (get-file-contents, never a cross-repo checkout; the sandbox has no cross-repo git). The canon PR is opened over MCP too.
    12	- **A member's local packs** are everything under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename window) — its own packs, never the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under `.claudinite/`.
    13	- **`main`** stands for the canon's default branch.
    14	
    15	## What each run does
    16	
    17	### 1. Read the target members' local **packs**
    18	
    19	For each member named in Context, read its **local packs**. The candidate pool is a local pack's captured knowledge — its `RULES.md` **prose** AND its own **checks** (a `<pack>/*.mjs` rule module — its id, description, and failure message *are* a captured, enforceable lesson; the strongest promotion lifts it to a **canon check**, generalized, reusing the [prose-to-checks](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) mechanics — or to canon prose when it doesn't generalize to a check). **Out of scope, staying put:** a lesson deliberately placed as a **code comment at its call site**, a project's task scripts, product source, and config. Never promote from product source. A genuinely portable rule that looks trapped in a code comment was mis-placed at extract time — leave it for a future extract pass to re-home into a pack. You don't need to tell new from old — the dedup step drops anything the canon already carries. No barrier holds tonight's extracts: read whatever is already **merged** on each member's default branch; anything landing mid-run is tomorrow's input.
    20	
    21	### 2. Generalize each candidate — *before* judging whether it belongs
    22	
    23	Generalize first, then decide worthiness — never the reverse. The act of generalizing is itself the portability probe — a rule that goes vacuous when lifted, or only makes sense with its project's context, isn't portable; leave it local. Work the rule standalone (origin naming and grouping carry no weight); strip the project (names, files, example stay in the origin repo — promote the distilled rule only); a **technology** mention isn't a disqualifier (lift it to the broadest scope that stays true — tech-specific is fine, *product*-specific is not); decide tool-vs-process and frame it for that home.
    24	
    25	### 3. Then judge worthiness — deduped against the *entire* corpus
    26	
    27	Holding the generalized rule, decide if it earns a place by the bar [item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) owns (don't restate its gates). Lean **inclusive** — keep anything a future project could use — but be strict about **duplication**: dedupe against **every** corpus doc, not only the one you'd expect to own it.
    28	
    29	### 4. Triage the mechanism, then route
    30	
    31	- **Descend the promotion ladder first** ([item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md)'s mechanism triage). Prose is the fallback, not the default: a lesson a check can carry is **authored as the check** in this PR — the rule module in the right pack, the failure message carrying the generalized lesson, **plus a fixture test proving it fires** on a violating input and stays quiet on a clean one. When a confident detection-plus-fixture can't be authored unattended, land the lesson as prose **and** open a tagged conformance-backlog issue — never a silently-shipped broken check.
    32	- **Route** each prose rule to its **one** owning doc ([item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) owns the placement); match its voice and format; pick exactly one owner, never split or duplicate.
    33	- **A technology with no home → mint a fingerprinted stub pack, in its own PR**, reusing the pack-writing mechanics [the generate-project-instructions skill](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md) owns — `packs/<tech>/` with `pack.mjs` (add the `marker`/`detect` fingerprint when the technology carries a reliable one, else `detect: null`), a `RULES.md` seeded from the lesson, a `README.md`, and its `packs/README.md` index row. A minted pack ships in its **own** PR, split from the run's lesson-promotion PR (a new pack earns its own review surface). Never mint from imagination and never park an empty one to fill later — a pack minted here is populated from the *real, portable lesson* that justified it. Do not pad it with speculative rules no project earned — the "written from imagination, not distilled from worked examples" failure; an ungroundable rule isn't written. (Authoring a *fuller* pack from a technology's usage across the whole fleet — rather than a single lesson — is the per-repo pack-discovery task's job, not this floor's.) The follow-ups a fresh stub invites — enriching it from known best practices, triaging which skills it should require, spinning up dependent/aspect packs — are **not** automated here: note them for the owner and leave them to a later, deliberate pass.
    34	- **Write it terse — when + what.** State the relevance (*when* it applies) and the rule (*what* to do); add a *why* only to flag severity, in a few words.
    35	- **Bounded write surface — `packs/`/`skills/` only** (CI-enforced on the PR). Edit only the one owning doc — or, for a check-conversion, only the new rule module, its registration in the pack registry, and its fixture test. Don't "improve" unrelated rules while you're in there. The two bounded exceptions (both within `packs/`): the new-doc path [item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) owns, and minting a stub pack.
    36	- **Open a PR against `main`** on a per-run-unique branch — one PR for the whole run's accepted lessons (a minted stub is the exception: its own PR). Never a direct push. Keep every commit and PR terse. **Put the issue reference in the commit message** (`Refs #<n>` for the tracker below) — the `basics` `task-lifecycle` check reds CI on a promote commit that cites none.
    37	
    38	### 5. Log the run to the tracker
    39	
    40	Append a dated comment for every run that promoted at least one lesson, and for any notable rejection.
    41	
    42	## Tracking issue
    43	
    44	The standing self-improvement log is the issue titled exactly **`Claudinite tracker: Promote to Canon`**.
    45	
    46	- **Find it by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number** (a bare number can dangle).
    47	- **Create it already closed if missing. Never open, close, or reopen it** — its state carries no meaning; only the log does.
    48	- Log each run as a **dated comment** — not a sub-issue, so history accumulates in one scrollable feed — the date, and per lesson: the origin repo, the **ladder rung it landed on** (check id / skill / owning doc, with the named reason when prose was the fallback), and the generalized rule (or, for a notable rejection, the reason and the existing rule that already covers it).
    49	
    50	## What this task must never do
    51	
    52	- **Never mine outside a local pack** — product source, task scripts, code comments, and config are out of scope; only a local pack's `RULES.md` prose and its own check modules are candidates.
    53	- **Never promote a product-specific or one-off item** — it stays in that project's local packs.
    54	- **Never weaken, restate, or duplicate an existing rule** — fold a genuine sharpening in per [item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) instead.
    55	- **Never widen past the Context member list**, and **never touch a member repo** — this task only reads members and writes the canon PR.
    56	- **Run on `opus`** — every step is a judgment call (portability, duplication, ownership, how to generalize without distorting), and a downgraded model ships a plausible-but-wrong *acceptance* the owner's review is least likely to catch. This task declares `agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.

     1	# Growth — discover canon packs (the fleet sweep)
     2	
     3	One weekly pass over **every member**: read what the fleet is actually built on, subtract what the shared canon already homes, and open a PR **for the owner to approve** authoring the pack that is missing. Declared only by Claudinite, so it runs **once, centrally**, never per project.
     4	
     5	This is the only thing that notices a technology in use across the fleet with **no canon pack**. Its per-repo namesake in [grow_with_claudinite](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md) is the other side of the same line: that one authors a repo's **own local** packs and is barred from re-creating what a canon pack homes. It cannot close a canon gap; you can, and only you.
     6	
     7	**Why central.** One run sees every member, so **first-sight dedup is free**: the third member using a technology is recognised as the same gap as the first, in the same pass, with no cross-run state and no chance of three repos each proposing the same pack.
     8	
     9	You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent-fleet` issue whose **Context section is binding scope**: it names the exact members to sweep. Work exactly that list — the fleet enumeration already happened in the precondition; **do not enumerate the fleet yourself or widen past the Context**. Finding nothing unhomed is a perfectly good, common outcome.
    10	
    11	The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`open-pr`**: a new canon pack is read by every repo that declares it, so it opens a PR and **never arms auto-merge** — the owner approves it.
    12	
    13	## Conventions used in this doc
    14	
    15	- **GitHub access is MCP-only** (`mcp__github__*`). You are outside each member repo — read its files over the API (get-file-contents, never a cross-repo checkout; the sandbox has no cross-repo git). The Claudinite PR is opened over MCP too.
    16	- **`main`** stands for Claudinite's default branch.
    17	- **The canon shelf** is Claudinite's own `packs/` tree — the packs every member can declare.
    18	
    19	## What each run does
    20	
    21	### 1. Manifest each member's stack
    22	
    23	For each member named in Context, catalogue what it is built on, exactly as the per-repo task's [manifest step](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md) specifies — the same three axes, the same per-item fields, the same **never infer from "projects like this usually…"** rule, the same comprehensive-over-concise bias. That step owns the method; do not re-derive or re-state it here. The only adaptation: you read the member over the API rather than a working checkout, and you keep one manifest **per member**, tagged with the repo it came from.
    24	
    25	Do not consult the canon shelf yet, and decide nothing about packs — this step only observes.
    26	
    27	### 2. Fold the members into one fleet view
    28	
    29	Merge the per-member manifests into a single list of technologies, keyed by the technology, each carrying **which members use it** and at what prominence. This fold is the whole reason the task is central: the same technology seen in four members is **one** entry, recognised on first sight, so there is no cross-run dedup state and no duplicate proposal.
    30	
    31	Drop anything no member uses at `core` or `supporting` prominence — a technology only some member's vestigial config mentions has taught the fleet nothing.
    32	
    33	### 3. Find the canon gap
    34	
    35	Hold the fleet view against the **canon shelf**. A candidate is a technology (or a domain the fleet shares) that:
    36	
    37	- **no canon pack homes** — and, per the per-repo task's rule, **a stub pack counts as homed**: if `packs/` already has any pack owning it, the gap is closed. The action for a member using a homed technology without declaring its pack is to note that ("member X should declare pack Y"), never to author a second pack; **and**
    38	- carries **real, portable working knowledge** the members actually demonstrate — a build/config gotcha, a toolchain rule, a procedure that recurs across them. Judge worthiness by the bar [item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) owns; don't restate its gates.
    39	
    40	Prefer a candidate **more than one member** uses — that is the evidence a pack is portable rather than one repo's local business. A single-member technology can still qualify when the knowledge is plainly general, but it is the weaker case, and the per-repo task already covers the local-pack answer.
    41	
    42	### 4. Author the pack — from the members' real usage
    43	
    44	Author `packs/<name>/` using the pack-writing mechanics [the generate-project-instructions skill](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md) owns — descend the promotion ladder, add the `marker`/`detect` fingerprint when the technology carries a reliable one (`detect: null` otherwise), write `RULES.md`/`pack.mjs`/`README.md`, and add its `packs/README.md` index row. Apply that method; do not re-derive it.
    45	
    46	Two rules from the per-repo task carry over unchanged, and are the ones this task most easily breaks because it is writing from *other* repos' evidence:
    47	
    48	- **Ground every rule in a member's real files, and cite which member.** Never author from imagination.
    49	- **Never pad** with speculative best-practice rules the evidence doesn't demonstrate, and **never open an empty stub to fill later**. A small honest pack beats a padded one; a rule you can't ground, you don't write.
    50	
    51	Strip the member (names, paths, and product concepts stay in the origin repo — a canon pack is written as if no particular repo existed); a technology mention is the point, a *product* mention is a defect.
    52	
    53	**One pack per PR.** A new pack earns its own review surface, so a run that finds two gaps opens two PRs.
    54	
    55	### 5. Open the PR
    56	
    57	Open a PR against `main` on a per-run-unique branch — never a direct push. Write surface is **`packs/` only**: the new pack's files and the `packs/README.md` index row. Don't "improve" unrelated packs while you're in there. Keep every commit and PR terse, and **put the issue reference in the commit message** (`Refs #<n>` for the tracker below), in the commit itself and not only the PR body.
    58	
    59	### 6. Log the run to the tracker
    60	
    61	The standing log is the issue titled exactly **`Claudinite tracker: Discover Canon Packs`**.
    62	
    63	- **Find it by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number** (a bare number can dangle).
    64	- **Create it already closed if missing. Never open, close, or reopen it** — its state carries no meaning; only the log does.
    65	- Log every run as a **dated comment**: the members swept; each pack authored (technology, the members that evidenced it, the rungs its rules landed on); each "member X should declare existing pack Y" note; and, for a candidate you rejected, its name and why. "Nothing unhomed this run" is worth a line too.
    66	
    67	## What this task must never do
    68	
    69	- **Never widen past the Context member list**, and **never touch a member repo** — this task only reads members and writes the Claudinite PR.
    70	- **Never author a pack for a technology the canon already homes** — a stub counts as homed; note the "declare the existing pack" action instead.
    71	- **Never author from imagination or pad, and never open an empty stub** — every rule traces to a named member's real files.
    72	- **Never write a member's product names, paths, or concepts into a canon pack** — that is the local-pack answer, and it belongs to the per-repo task.
    73	- **Never write outside `packs/`** — no engine, no docs, no member-side change.
    74	- **Run on `opus`** — every step is a judgment call (is this technology genuinely unhomed, has the fleet earned a shared pack for it, what does the evidence actually support), and you are authoring from *other* repos' evidence with no owner able to re-derive each call. This task declares `agent_model: opus`.
